name: Roast chicken
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and let the chicken come to room temperature for 30 minutes.
Rub the butter, olive oil, thyme, salt and pepper all over the skin.
Stuff the cavity with the lemon, garlic and onion, then sit the chicken in a roasting tin.
Roast for 1 hour 20 minutes, basting once, until the juices run clear when the thigh is pierced.
Rest under foil for 20 minutes before carving, and use the tin juices for gravy.

name: Roast beef
steps: Take the beef out of the fridge an hour before cooking and heat the oven to 220C.
Mix the mustard powder, flour, salt and pepper and rub over the beef with the oil.
Sit the beef on the sliced onions in a roasting tin and roast for 20 minutes.
Lower the oven to 180C and roast for a further 15 minutes per 500g for medium-rare.
Rest the beef under foil for at least 30 minutes, then carve thinly.

name: Roast leg of lamb
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and take the lamb out of the fridge for 30 minutes.
Make small cuts all over the lamb and push in the garlic slices and small pieces of rosemary.
Rub with olive oil, salt and pepper and sit on the onions in a roasting tin.
Roast for 20 minutes, then lower to 180C and cook for about 1 hour 30 minutes for pink, longer for well done.
Pour in the wine for the last 30 minutes, then rest the lamb for 20 minutes before carving.

name: Roast pork with crackling
ingredients: 2kg pork shoulder or loin, skin scored
steps: Dry the pork skin well with kitchen paper and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight if you can.
Heat the oven to 240C. Rub the oil, salt and fennel seeds into the scored skin.
Sit the pork on the onions and apples in a tin and roast for 30 minutes until the skin blisters.
Lower to 180C and roast for a further 2 hours until the meat is tender.
Rest for 20 minutes, snap off the crackling and carve the meat.

name: Roast turkey
steps: Heat the oven to 190C. Rub the butter, salt and pepper over the turkey and put the lemon and onions in the cavity.
Lay the bacon over the breast and sit the turkey in a large roasting tin.
Cover loosely with foil and roast for about 3 hours 15 minutes, basting every 45 minutes.
Remove the foil for the last 40 minutes so the skin browns and the juices run clear.
Rest under foil for 45 minutes before carving.

name: Roast potatoes
ingredients: 1.2kg Maris Piper potatoes, peeled and halved
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and put the oil in a roasting tin to heat up.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 10 minutes, then drain and let them steam dry for 5 minutes.
Shake the pan to roughen the edges and toss with the flour and salt.
Carefully tip the potatoes into the hot oil, turn to coat and roast for 50 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and crisp.

name: Yorkshire puddings
steps: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and salt into a smooth batter and rest for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 230C. Put 1 tbsp of oil into each hole of a 6-hole muffin tin and heat until smoking.
Pour the batter quickly into the hot oil, filling each hole about two-thirds full.
Bake for 20 minutes without opening the oven until puffed and golden, then serve straight away.

name: Roast dinner gravy
steps: Pour off most of the fat from the roasting tin, leaving about 2 tbsp of juices behind.
Place the tin on the hob over a medium heat, stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in the hot water with the crumbled stock cube, scraping up the sticky bits.
Add the Worcestershire sauce and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until thickened, then season and strain.

name: Sage and onion stuffing
steps: Heat the oven to 190C. Soften the onions in the butter for 8 minutes and leave to cool.
Mix the onions with the breadcrumbs, sage, sausagemeat, egg and the crumbled stock cube.
Season well, then press into a greased baking dish.
Bake for 35 minutes until golden and crisp on top.

name: Pigs in blankets
steps: Heat the oven to 200C.
Stretch each bacon rasher with the back of a knife and wrap it tightly around a chipolata.
Place on a lined baking tray, drizzle with the oil and honey if using.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until the bacon is crisp and the sausages cooked through.

name: Cauliflower cheese
steps: Heat the oven to 200C. Boil the florets for 5 minutes, then drain well.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk gradually.
Simmer for 5 minutes until thick, then stir in two thirds of the cheddar, mustard, nutmeg and seasoning.
Tip the cauliflower into a baking dish, pour over the sauce and top with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 20 minutes until bubbling and golden.

name: Braised red cabbage
steps: Melt the butter in a large pan with a lid and soften the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the cabbage, apples, vinegar, sugar, mixed spice and seasoning and stir well.
Cover and cook over a very low heat for about 1 hour, stirring occasionally, adding a splash of water if it dries out.
Taste and adjust the sugar and vinegar before serving.

name: Honey-roast parsnips
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and put the oil in a roasting tin to heat.
Parboil the parsnips for 5 minutes, drain and leave to steam dry.
Toss in the hot oil and roast for 25 minutes until starting to colour.
Mix the honey and mustard, drizzle over the parsnips with the thyme and roast for 15 minutes more until sticky.

name: Shepherd's pie
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes, then mash with the butter and milk.
Fry the mince in a large pan until browned, then add the onion and carrots and cook for 8 minutes.
Stir in the flour, tomato puree and Worcestershire sauce, then add the crumbled stock cube and 300ml boiling water.
Simmer for 25 minutes, adding the peas for the last 5, then tip into a baking dish.
Top with the mash, rough up with a fork and bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden.

name: Cottage pie
steps: Boil the potatoes for 20 minutes, drain and mash with the butter and milk.
Brown the mince in a large pan, then add the onion and carrots and cook for 8 minutes.
Stir in the flour, tomato puree, Worcestershire sauce and the crumbled stock cube with 300ml boiling water.
Simmer for 25 minutes until thick and tip into a baking dish.
Spread over the mash, sprinkle with cheddar and bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden.

name: Fish and chips
ingredients: 1kg Maris Piper potatoes, cut into thick chips
steps: Soak the chips in cold water for 15 minutes, drain and dry thoroughly.
Heat the oil to 140C and fry the chips for 8 minutes until soft but pale. Drain.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and sparkling water into a thick batter.
Heat the oil to 190C. Dust the fish in flour, dip in batter and fry for 6 to 8 minutes until golden, then drain.
Fry the chips again for 3 to 4 minutes until crisp, salt well and serve with the fish and lemon.

name: Bangers and mash with onion gravy
steps: Boil the potatoes for 20 minutes, drain and mash with half the butter and the milk.
Fry or grill the sausages for 20 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Fry the onions in the oil and remaining butter for 15 minutes until deep golden.
Stir in the flour, then add 400ml boiling water with the crumbled stock cube and the Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer for 8 minutes until thick and serve over the sausages and mash.

name: Toad in the hole
steps: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and salt into a smooth batter and rest for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220C. Put the sausages and oil in a roasting tin and cook for 10 minutes.
Pour the hot tin batter over the sausages quickly, scatter in the onion and return to the oven.
Bake for 30 minutes without opening the door until risen and golden. Serve with gravy.

name: Full English breakfast
steps: Grill or fry the sausages for 15 minutes, turning, until cooked through.
Add the bacon, black pudding, tomatoes and mushrooms to the pan or grill and cook for about 8 minutes.
Warm the beans in a small pan.
Fry the eggs in the oil to your liking and toast the bread, then butter it.
Plate everything up together and serve hot.

name: Beef stew and dumplings
steps: Toss the beef in the plain flour and brown in batches in the oil in a large casserole.
Add the onions and carrots, then the tomato puree, Worcestershire sauce, bay leaf and the stock cube with 700ml boiling water.
Cover and cook at 160C for 2 hours until the beef is tender.
Mix the self-raising flour, suet, a pinch of salt and about 90ml cold water into a dough and shape into 8 balls.
Place the dumplings on top of the stew, cover and cook for 25 minutes more until fluffy.

name: Lancashire hotpot
steps: Heat the oven to 160C. Brown the lamb in the oil, then stir in the flour.
Layer the lamb, onions and carrots into a casserole, adding the bay leaf and Worcestershire sauce.
Pour over 400ml boiling water mixed with the crumbled stock cube.
Arrange the potato slices over the top in overlapping layers and brush with the melted butter.
Cover and bake for 2 hours, then uncover and cook for 30 minutes more until the potatoes are golden.

name: Steak and ale pie
steps: Toss the beef in flour and brown in batches in the oil in a casserole.
Add the onions, mushrooms, ale, Worcestershire sauce and the stock cube with 200ml boiling water.
Cover and cook at 160C for 2 hours until tender, then cool slightly and tip into a pie dish.
Roll out the pastry, cover the dish and trim, then brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 200C for 30 minutes until puffed and golden.

name: Steak and kidney pudding
steps: Toss the beef and kidney in the plain flour with salt and pepper.
Mix the self-raising flour, suet, a pinch of salt and about 180ml cold water into a dough. Roll out and use two thirds to line a greased 1.2l pudding basin.
Fill with the meat, onion, mushrooms and Worcestershire sauce, then pour in 250ml hot water with the crumbled stock cube.
Roll out the remaining dough for a lid, seal the edges and cover with pleated foil and baking paper tied with string.
Steam over simmering water for 4 hours, topping up the water as needed, then turn out to serve.

name: Chicken and leek pie
steps: Soften the leeks in the butter for 8 minutes, then add the chicken and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour, then gradually add the milk and crumbled stock cube and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the mustard and cream, season well and tip into a pie dish to cool a little.
Cover with the rolled-out pastry, trim, make a steam hole and brush with egg.
Bake at 200C for 30 minutes until the pastry is golden and puffed.

name: Chicken kiev
steps: Mash the butter with the garlic, parsley and seasoning, shape into a log and chill for 30 minutes.
Cut a deep pocket into each chicken breast and push in a quarter of the garlic butter, then secure with a cocktail stick.
Coat each breast in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
Place on a lined tray and bake at 200C for 30 minutes until golden and cooked through. Remove the sticks before serving.

name: Gammon, egg and chips
steps: Heat the oven to 220C. Toss the chips in 1 tbsp of oil and salt and roast for 30 minutes, turning once.
Snip the gammon fat in a few places and fry in the butter for 4 to 5 minutes each side.
Boil the peas for 3 minutes and drain.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil, then serve everything together.

name: Liver and onions
steps: Fry the bacon until crisp, remove, then cook the onions in the butter and oil for 15 minutes until golden. Set aside.
Toss the liver in the seasoned flour and fry for 2 minutes each side until just pink inside, then remove.
Stir 1 tbsp of the remaining flour into the pan, add 250ml boiling water with the crumbled stock cube and the Worcestershire sauce.
Return the onions and liver to the gravy for 1 minute and serve with mash and the bacon.

name: Corned beef hash
steps: Boil the potatoes for 8 minutes until just tender, then drain.
Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the potatoes and cook until golden.
Break up the corned beef and stir it in with the Worcestershire sauce and brown sauce.
Cook for 10 minutes, pressing down and turning, until crisp and browned. Season and serve.

name: Bubble and squeak
steps: Soften the onion in 1 tbsp of oil for 5 minutes.
Mix the onion with the mash, cabbage and seasoning in a bowl.
Heat the remaining oil and butter in a frying pan and press in the mixture into a flat cake.
Fry over a medium heat for 8 minutes until browned and crisp, flip and cook the other side for 6 minutes.

name: Welsh rarebit
steps: Melt the butter in a small pan, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then add the ale or milk.
Stir in the cheddar, mustard and Worcestershire sauce until melted, then beat in the egg yolk off the heat.
Toast the bread on one side under the grill, then spread the mixture over the other side.
Grill for 3 to 4 minutes until bubbling and golden.

name: Cullen skink
steps: Poach the haddock in the milk and water for 6 minutes, then lift out and flake, discarding skin and bones. Keep the liquid.
Soften the onion in the butter for 5 minutes, then add the potatoes and the poaching liquid.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender, then mash roughly with a fork to thicken.
Stir in the flaked fish and parsley, warm through and season with black pepper.

name: Haggis, neeps and tatties
steps: Wrap the haggis in foil and bake at 180C for 1 hour (or simmer in its casing for 50 minutes).
Boil the swede for 25 minutes and the potatoes for 20 minutes in separate pans.
Mash the swede with half the butter, nutmeg and seasoning.
Mash the potatoes with the remaining butter and the milk.
Serve the haggis sliced with the neeps and tatties.

name: Scotch broth
steps: Put the lamb, barley, split peas and water in a large pan and bring to the boil, skimming off any scum.
Simmer gently for 1 hour.
Add the onion, carrots, swede and leek and simmer for 40 minutes more.
Lift out the lamb, shred the meat and return it to the pan with the parsley. Season and serve.

name: Cornish pasty
steps: Rub the flour, butter and lard together with a pinch of salt, add about 150ml cold water and bring together into a dough. Chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220C. Divide the dough into 4 and roll each into a 20cm circle.
Mix the beef, potatoes, swede, onion, salt and plenty of pepper and pile onto one half of each circle.
Brush the edges with egg, fold over and crimp firmly to seal. Brush with more egg.
Bake for 20 minutes, then reduce to 180C and bake for 40 minutes more until golden.

name: Pork pie
steps: Heat the lard with 200ml water until melted, then mix into the flour and salt to make a warm dough.
Line a 20cm springform tin with two thirds of the dough, keeping the rest warm for the lid.
Mix the pork, mace, pepper and salt and pack firmly into the case, then add the lid, seal and make a hole in the top. Brush with egg.
Bake at 200C for 30 minutes, then at 160C for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Soften the gelatine in the warm stock, pour through the hole and chill overnight before slicing.

name: Sausage rolls
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and line a baking tray.
Mix the sausage meat with the onion, sage, mustard and pepper.
Roll out the pastry into a long rectangle, cut in half lengthways and pipe or shape the filling down the centre of each strip.
Brush the edge with egg, fold over, seal and cut into 6 pieces. Brush the tops with egg.
Bake for 25 minutes until puffed, golden and cooked through.

name: Scotch eggs
steps: Boil the 6 eggs for 6 minutes, cool in iced water and peel.
Mix the sausage meat with the sage, salt and pepper and divide into 6.
Flatten each portion, wrap around an egg and seal. Roll in flour, then the beaten egg, then breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil to 170C and fry two or three at a time for 6 minutes until deep golden, then drain.
Finish in a 180C oven for 8 minutes if the meat needs it, and cool before serving.

name: Kedgeree
steps: Cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10 minutes, drain and keep warm.
Poach the haddock in the milk for 6 minutes, then flake the fish, discarding the skin.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool, peel and quarter.
Soften the onion in the butter, stir in the curry powder, then add the rice and flaked fish.
Fold in the parsley and lemon juice and top with the eggs.

name: Coronation chicken
steps: Mix the mayonnaise, yoghurt, chutney, curry powder and lemon juice in a large bowl.
Fold in the chicken and sultanas until evenly coated.
Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Scatter with the almonds and serve in sandwiches, on jacket potatoes or with a green salad.

name: Ploughman's lunch
steps: Cut the cheddar into thick wedges and split the rolls.
Arrange the cheese, ham, rolls, pickles and butter on two boards or plates.
Add the tomatoes, apple and salad leaves.
Serve straight away with a spoonful of piccalilli.

name: Cheese and onion pie
steps: Boil the potatoes for 10 minutes until just tender and drain well.
Soften the onions in the butter for 10 minutes and leave to cool.
Mix the potatoes, onions, cheddar, cream and plenty of pepper.
Line a pie dish with the shortcrust, fill, cover with the puff pastry, seal and brush with egg.
Bake at 200C for 35 minutes until golden.

name: Mince and tatties
steps: Boil the potatoes for 20 minutes, drain and mash with the butter.
Brown the mince in a large pan, then add the onion and carrots and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour, Worcestershire sauce and the crumbled stock cube with 400ml boiling water.
Simmer for 25 minutes, adding the peas for the last 5 minutes, then serve beside the mash.

name: Stovies
ingredients: 300g leftover roast beef or lamb, chopped
steps: Melt the dripping in a heavy pan and fry the onions for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the meat and potatoes and stir to coat.
Dissolve the stock cube in the hot water and pour over, then season.
Cover and cook gently for 35 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potatoes are soft and starting to break down.

name: Irish stew
steps: Layer the lamb, onions, carrots and half the potatoes in a large heavy pot with the thyme and seasoning.
Dissolve the stock cube in the hot water and pour over, then cover and bring to a simmer.
Cook gently for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Add the remaining potatoes, which will thicken the stew, and cook for 30 minutes more.
Scatter with parsley and serve in deep bowls.

name: Colcannon
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes, then drain and mash.
Cook the cabbage in boiling water for 4 minutes and drain well.
Warm the milk with the spring onions for 3 minutes.
Beat the milk mixture, cabbage and most of the butter into the mash and season well.
Serve with a well of melted butter in the middle.

name: Champ
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes and drain.
Simmer the spring onions in the milk for 3 minutes.
Mash the potatoes, then beat in the hot milk and onions and half the butter.
Season well and serve with the rest of the butter melting on top.

name: Boxty
steps: Grate the raw potatoes, squeeze out the liquid in a clean tea towel and put in a bowl.
Mix in the mashed potato, flour, baking powder, egg and enough buttermilk to make a thick batter. Season.
Heat the oil and butter in a frying pan and spoon in the batter in pancake-sized rounds.
Fry for 4 to 5 minutes each side until golden and cooked through.

name: Glamorgan sausages
steps: Soften the leek in 1 tbsp of oil for 5 minutes and cool.
Mix 100g of the breadcrumbs with the cheese, leek, parsley, mustard and one whole egg plus one yolk.
Shape into 8 small sausages and chill for 15 minutes.
Roll the sausages in flour, dip in the remaining egg white, then coat in the remaining breadcrumbs.
Fry in the remaining oil for 8 minutes, turning, until golden.

name: Beef Wellington
steps: Season the beef and sear in the hot oil for 1 minute on each side. Brush with the mustard and cool.
Fry the mushrooms with the butter and thyme for 10 minutes until dry, then cool.
Lay the Parma ham on cling film, spread over the mushrooms, roll the beef in it and chill for 30 minutes.
Wrap the beef in the rolled-out pastry, seal the edges, brush with egg yolk and chill for 20 minutes.
Bake at 200C for 35 minutes for medium-rare, then rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

name: Chicken chasseur
steps: Brown the chicken skin side down in the oil in a casserole for 8 minutes, then remove.
Fry the onion and mushrooms in the same pan for 6 minutes, then add the garlic and tomato puree.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble, then add the tomatoes, tarragon and the crumbled stock cube with 150ml hot water.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer for 35 minutes until cooked through and the sauce has thickened.

name: Pork chops with apple sauce
steps: Cook the apples with the sugar and water in a covered pan for 10 minutes until collapsed, then beat smooth with a little butter.
Season the chops and score the fat.
Fry in the oil for 5 minutes on each side, adding the remaining butter and spooning it over.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve with the apple sauce.

name: Lamb chops with mint sauce
steps: Dissolve the sugar in the boiling water, add the mint and vinegar and leave to infuse for 15 minutes.
Rub the chops with the oil, salt and pepper.
Grill or fry for 4 to 5 minutes each side for pink, or longer if you prefer.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve with the mint sauce.

name: Chicken carcass soup
steps: Put the carcass in a large pan with half the onion and carrot, the bay leaf and 2 litres of water.
Simmer for 1 hour 30 minutes, then strain and discard the bones.
Return the stock to the pan with the remaining vegetables and the barley and simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the shredded chicken and parsley, heat through and season.

name: Leftover turkey curry
steps: Fry the onions in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and curry powder and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato puree, tomatoes, hot water, crumbled stock cube and chutney and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the turkey and simmer for 10 minutes until piping hot.
Cook the rice according to the pack and serve with the curry.

name: Turkey and ham pie
steps: Soften the leek in the butter for 6 minutes, then stir in the flour.
Whisk in the milk and crumbled stock cube and simmer for 6 minutes until thick, then add the cream.
Fold in the turkey and ham, season and tip into a pie dish.
Cover with the pastry, trim, brush with egg and bake at 200C for 30 minutes until golden.

name: Chip shop curry sauce
steps: Fry the onion in the oil for 10 minutes until very soft, then add the garlic, curry powder and turmeric and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the flour, then gradually add the hot water and crumbled stock cube.
Add the chutney and sugar and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Blend until smooth if you like, and serve over chips.

name: Mushy peas
steps: Put the peas, water and sugar in a pan and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the butter and mint sauce.
Mash roughly with a fork or potato masher, season and serve.

name: Pease pudding
steps: Soak the split peas in cold water overnight and drain.
Put them in a pan with the onion, carrot and fresh water and bring to the boil.
Simmer for about 1 hour 30 minutes until the peas are completely soft.
Drain, discard the vegetables and beat the peas with the butter, salt and pepper until thick and creamy.

name: Faggots
steps: Heat the oven to 180C. Mix the pork, liver, onion, breadcrumbs, sage, mace and seasoning.
Shape into 8 balls and place in a baking dish.
Dissolve the stock cube and Worcestershire sauce in the hot water, whisk in the flour and pour around the faggots.
Bake for 1 hour, turning once, until browned and the gravy has thickened. Serve with mash and peas.

name: Fried black pudding with apple
steps: Melt half the butter in a frying pan and cook the apple slices with the sugar for 3 minutes until caramelised. Set aside.
Fry the black pudding in the remaining butter for 2 to 3 minutes on each side until crisp.
Toast the bread and serve topped with the black pudding and apple.

name: Black pudding hash
steps: Boil the potatoes for 6 minutes and drain.
Fry the onion and potatoes in the oil for 10 minutes until golden.
Add the black pudding and cook for 5 minutes, stirring in the brown sauce.
Make two hollows, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 4 minutes until set.

name: Bacon and cabbage
steps: Cover the bacon with cold water in a large pan with the onion, carrots and bay leaf and bring to the boil, then pour off the water.
Cover with fresh water and simmer for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Add the potatoes for the last 25 minutes and the cabbage for the last 10 minutes.
Lift out the bacon and slice, then serve with the vegetables, butter and mustard.

name: Boiled ham with parsley sauce
steps: Soak the gammon in cold water for 2 hours if salty, then drain.
Cover with fresh water, add the onion, carrots and bay leaf, then simmer for 2 hours.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and gradually whisk in the milk to make a smooth sauce.
Simmer for 5 minutes, add the parsley and season, then slice the ham and serve with the sauce.

name: Devilled kidneys
steps: Toast the bread and keep warm.
Fry the kidneys in the butter over a high heat for 3 minutes, turning.
Stir in the Worcestershire sauce, mustard and cayenne and cook for 1 minute.
Add the cream, simmer for 2 minutes and spoon over the toast.

name: Potted shrimp
steps: Melt the butter gently and skim off any foam.
Stir in the mace, cayenne and lemon juice, then fold in the shrimps.
Spoon into 4 small pots and pour the remaining butter on top.
Chill for at least 2 hours and serve with hot toast.

name: Dressed crab
ingredients: 300g fresh white and brown crab meat
steps: Mix the brown crab meat with the mayonnaise, mustard and half the lemon juice.
Season the white crab meat with the remaining lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Spoon the brown meat into the middle of 2 plates or crab shells and the white meat on each side.
Sprinkle with egg and parsley and serve with buttered brown bread.

name: Bread sauce
steps: Put the onion halves, ground cloves and bay leaf in a pan with the milk.
Heat gently until almost boiling, then leave to infuse for 20 minutes.
Remove the onion and bay leaf, stir in the breadcrumbs and simmer for 5 minutes until thick.
Beat in the butter, cream, nutmeg and salt to taste.

name: Mashed potato
ingredients: 1kg Maris Piper potatoes, peeled and chopped
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 18 to 20 minutes until completely tender.
Drain well and let them steam dry for 2 minutes.
Mash until smooth, then beat in the butter and warm milk.
Season and serve straight away.

name: Mashed swede and carrot
steps: Boil the swede and carrots together in salted water for 20 minutes until very tender.
Drain well and steam dry in the pan for 2 minutes.
Mash with the butter, nutmeg and plenty of pepper and serve hot.

name: Brussels sprouts with bacon
steps: Boil the sprouts for 4 minutes and drain.
Fry the bacon in the oil until crisp.
Add the butter and sprouts and toss over a high heat for 4 minutes until lightly browned.
Stir in the chestnuts if using, season and serve.

name: Creamed leeks
steps: Melt the butter in a pan, add the leeks and cook gently for 8 minutes until soft.
Pour in the cream and mustard and simmer for 5 minutes until thickened.
Season well and serve with roast meats or fish.

name: Chunky chips
ingredients: 1kg Maris Piper potatoes, cut into thick chips
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and put a large tray in to heat.
Parboil the chips for 5 minutes, drain and steam dry for 5 minutes.
Toss with the oil, paprika and garlic cloves on the hot tray and roast for 35 to 40 minutes, turning twice, until crisp and golden.
Sprinkle with sea salt and serve immediately.

name: Beer-battered onion rings
steps: Whisk 125g of the flour, baking powder, salt and lager into a smooth batter.
Heat the oil to 180C.
Toss the onion rings in the remaining flour, dip into the batter and fry in batches for 3 minutes until golden.
Drain on kitchen paper and serve hot.

name: Scampi and chips
steps: Heat the oil to 180C and fry the chips for 8 to 10 minutes until crisp, then drain and salt.
Fry the scampi in batches for 2 to 3 minutes until golden, or cook from frozen per the pack.
Boil the peas for 3 minutes.
Serve with the lemon and tartare sauce.

name: Chicken and mushroom pie
steps: Fry the chicken in half the butter for 5 minutes, then add the onion and mushrooms and cook for 8 minutes.
Stir in the remaining butter and the flour, then gradually add the milk and crumbled stock cube.
Add the thyme and simmer for 10 minutes. Cool a little and tip into a pie dish.
Cover with the pastry, brush with egg and bake at 200C for 30 minutes until golden.

name: Sausage casserole
steps: Brown the sausages in the oil in a casserole and set aside.
Fry the onion, carrots and mushrooms in the same pan for 8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, tomato puree, Worcestershire sauce and the crumbled stock cube with 200ml boiling water.
Return the sausages and simmer for 30 minutes, adding the butter beans for the last 10, until the sauce has thickened.

name: Oxtail stew
steps: Toss the oxtail in the flour and brown well in batches in the oil in a casserole.
Soften the onions and carrots in the same pan, then stir in the tomato puree.
Add the wine, Worcestershire sauce, bay leaves and the crumbled stock cube with 500ml boiling water, then return the oxtail.
Cover and cook at 160C for 3 hours 30 minutes until the meat falls from the bone.
Skim off the fat and serve with mash.

name: Braised steak and onions
steps: Heat the oven to 160C. Season the flour and coat the steak.
Brown the steak in the oil, then transfer to a casserole.
Soften the onions in the pan for 10 minutes and add to the steak with the tomato puree, Worcestershire sauce and bay leaf.
Pour in 500ml hot water with the crumbled stock cube, cover and cook for 2 hours until tender.

name: Cumberland pie
steps: Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes and mash with half the butter.
Brown the mince, add the onion and carrots and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the tomato puree, Worcestershire sauce and crumbled stock cube with 300ml boiling water and simmer for 20 minutes.
Tip into a dish, cover with the mash, then top with the breadcrumbs mixed with the cheese and dot with the remaining butter.
Bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden.

name: Braised lamb shanks
steps: Heat the oven to 160C. Brown the shanks all over in the oil in a casserole and set aside.
Soften the onions, carrots and garlic in the same pot, then stir in the tomato puree.
Add the wine, redcurrant jelly, rosemary and the crumbled stock cube with 500ml boiling water.
Return the shanks, cover and cook for 2 hours 30 minutes, turning once, until the meat is very tender.
Serve with mash and the reduced sauce.

name: Scouse
steps: Brown the lamb in the oil in a large pot and add the onions.
Add the carrots, half the potatoes, bay leaf, Worcestershire sauce and the crumbled stock cube with 800ml boiling water.
Simmer gently for 1 hour 15 minutes.
Add the remaining potatoes and cook for 30 minutes more until they have broken down to thicken the stew.

name: Welsh cawl
steps: Put the lamb, onion, stock cube and water in a large pan and bring to a simmer.
Cook gently for 1 hour 15 minutes, skimming off the scum.
Add the carrots, swede and potatoes and simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the leeks for the last 10 minutes, then lift out the bones, return the meat and stir in the parsley.

name: Leek and potato soup
steps: Melt the butter in a large pan and soften the leeks and onion for 10 minutes without browning.
Add the potatoes and the stock cube dissolved in the hot water.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the potatoes are soft, then blend until smooth.
Stir in the cream, season and warm through.

name: Cream of tomato soup
steps: Soften the onion and carrot in the oil for 10 minutes.
Stir in the tomato puree, then add the tomatoes, sugar and the stock cube dissolved in the hot water.
Simmer for 20 minutes and blend until smooth.
Stir in the cream, season and serve with crusty bread.

name: Pea and ham soup
steps: Rinse the split peas and put them in a large pan with the hock, onion, carrots, celery, bay leaf and water.
Bring to the boil, skim, then simmer for 2 hours until the peas have broken down.
Lift out the hock, shred the meat and discard the skin and bone.
Return the meat to the soup, add the parsley and season with pepper.

name: Bacon sandwich
steps: Grill or fry the bacon for 3 to 4 minutes each side until as crisp as you like.
Butter the bread.
Layer the bacon on 2 slices, add brown sauce and top with the other slices.
Cut in half and serve hot.

name: Beans on toast
steps: Warm the beans in a small pan with the Worcestershire sauce if using.
Toast the bread and butter it.
Spoon the beans over the toast and top with grated cheddar if you like.

name: Cheese on toast
steps: Toast the bread on one side under the grill and butter the untoasted side.
Mix the cheddar with the Worcestershire sauce and mustard and pile onto the buttered sides.
Grill for 3 to 4 minutes until bubbling and browned.

name: Scrambled eggs on toast
steps: Beat the eggs with the milk, salt and pepper.
Melt half the butter in a non-stick pan over a low heat and pour in the eggs.
Stir slowly with a spatula for 2 to 3 minutes until softly set.
Toast and butter the bread and pile the eggs on top.

name: Kippers
steps: Put the kippers in a deep jug or pan and cover with just-boiled water. Leave for 5 minutes.
Poach or fry the eggs.
Drain the kippers and serve with a knob of butter melted on top, the lemon juice, the eggs and buttered brown bread.

name: Macaroni cheese
steps: Cook the macaroni for 2 minutes less than the pack says and drain.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk gradually and simmer for 6 minutes.
Stir in most of the cheddar and the mustard, then fold in the pasta.
Tip into a baking dish, top with the tomatoes, breadcrumbs and remaining cheese.
Bake at 200C for 20 minutes until golden.

name: Chicken casserole
steps: Heat the oven to 180C. Brown the chicken in the oil in a casserole, then remove.
Fry the bacon, onion, carrots and mushrooms for 6 minutes, then stir in the flour.
Add 500ml boiling water with the crumbled stock cube, the thyme and the potatoes.
Return the chicken, cover and cook for 50 minutes until tender and the sauce has thickened.

name: Steak and chips with peppercorn sauce
steps: Roast the chips at 220C with 1 tbsp oil for 35 minutes, turning once.
Season the steaks and fry in the remaining oil over a high heat for 3 minutes each side for medium. Rest on a plate.
Add the butter and peppercorns to the pan, pour in the brandy and let it bubble.
Stir in the cream and crumbled stock cube and simmer for 3 minutes. Serve the sauce over the steaks with the chips.

name: Glazed baked gammon
steps: Put the gammon, onion and bay leaf in a pan, cover with cold water and simmer for 1 hour 30 minutes. Drain.
Heat the oven to 200C. Cut off the rind and score the fat in diamonds.
Mix the mustard, honey, sugar and cloves and brush over the fat.
Roast for 30 minutes, basting twice, until sticky and golden. Rest for 15 minutes before carving.

name: Bacon roly-poly
steps: Mix the flour, suet and salt with about 120ml cold water into a soft dough.
Roll into a 30 x 25cm rectangle on a floured surface.
Scatter over the bacon, onion and sage, leaving a border, and brush the edges with egg.
Roll up like a Swiss roll and wrap loosely in buttered baking paper, then in foil.
Steam above boiling water for 2 hours, then slice and serve with gravy.

name: Bacon and egg pie
steps: Heat the oven to 200C. Roll out two thirds of the pastry and line a 23cm pie dish.
Fry the bacon and onion in the oil for 8 minutes and cool slightly, then spread over the pastry.
Make 6 hollows and crack in 6 eggs, adding the parsley and pepper.
Cover with the remaining pastry, seal, trim and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 35 minutes until golden and serve warm or cold.

name: Homity pie
steps: Heat the oven to 200C. Line a 23cm tart tin with the pastry and bake blind for 15 minutes.
Boil the potatoes for 10 minutes and drain.
Soften the leeks, onion and garlic in the butter for 8 minutes, then add the thyme.
Mix with the potatoes, two thirds of the cheddar and the cream, season and pile into the case.
Top with the remaining cheese and bake at 190C for 25 minutes until golden.

name: Tattie scones
steps: Mix the mashed potato with the butter and salt.
Work in the flour to make a soft dough and roll out to 5mm thick.
Cut into rounds or triangles and prick with a fork.
Cook in a dry non-stick pan for 3 minutes each side until golden speckled.

name: Fish finger sandwich
steps: Cook the fish fingers in the oven at 200C for 15 to 18 minutes, turning once.
Butter the bread and spread tartare sauce on two slices.
Layer the fish fingers, lettuce and tomato and top with the remaining slices.
Squash gently and serve.

name: Cod in parsley sauce
steps: Poach the cod in the milk with the bay leaf for 8 minutes, then lift out and keep warm. Strain and keep the milk.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and gradually whisk in the warm milk.
Simmer for 5 minutes until thickened, then add the parsley, lemon juice and seasoning.
Pour the sauce over the cod and serve with potatoes.

name: Coleslaw
steps: Mix the mayonnaise, yoghurt, mustard and vinegar in a large bowl.
Add the cabbage, carrots and onion and toss well.
Season and chill for 30 minutes before serving.

name: Prawn cocktail
steps: Mix the mayonnaise, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce and half the lemon juice for the Marie Rose sauce.
Divide the lettuce between 4 glasses and top with the prawns.
Spoon the sauce over and dust with cayenne.
Serve with the remaining lemon and buttered brown bread.

name: Chicken liver pate
steps: Melt 25g of the butter and soften the onion and garlic for 6 minutes.
Add the livers and thyme and cook for 4 minutes until browned but still slightly pink inside.
Add the brandy and bubble for 1 minute.
Blend with 100g of the soft butter until smooth, season and spoon into ramekins.
Melt the remaining butter and pour over, then chill for 3 hours and serve with toast.

name: Smoked mackerel pate
steps: Flake the mackerel into a bowl, removing any bones.
Add the cream cheese, creme fraiche, lemon juice, horseradish and pepper.
Mash or blend to your preferred texture and chill for 1 hour.
Serve with hot toast and lemon wedges.

name: Minted peas
steps: Boil the peas with the sugar for 3 minutes and drain.
Toss with the butter and mint.
Season with salt and pepper and serve hot.

name: Pan haggerty
steps: Heat the butter and oil in a large ovenproof frying pan.
Layer in the potatoes, onions and cheddar, seasoning each layer, and finish with a layer of potato.
Cover with foil and cook over a low heat for 30 minutes.
Uncover, top with more cheese if you like, and grill for 5 minutes until golden.

name: Smoked haddock with poached egg
steps: Poach the haddock in the milk for 6 minutes, then drain and keep warm.
Poach the eggs in simmering water for 3 minutes.
Toast and butter the bread.
Serve the haddock on the toast topped with the eggs and parsley.

name: Fried whitebait
steps: Heat the oil to 190C.
Toss the whitebait in the flour mixed with cayenne and salt, shaking off the excess.
Fry in small batches for 2 minutes until crisp, then drain on kitchen paper.
Sprinkle with salt and serve with lemon wedges.

name: Pork and apple casserole
steps: Heat the oven to 160C. Toss the pork in the flour and brown in the oil in a casserole.
Add the onions, apples and sage and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the cider and 200ml boiling water with the crumbled stock cube and mustard.
Cover and cook for 1 hour 30 minutes until tender.
Stir in the cream and heat through.

name: Glazed carrots
steps: Boil the carrots for 6 minutes until just tender and drain.
Melt the butter and honey in the pan, return the carrots and toss over a medium heat for 3 minutes until glossy.
Season and scatter with parsley.

name: Spaghetti bolognese
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and soften the onion and carrot for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and mince and fry over a high heat until browned all over.
Stir in the tomato puree, chopped tomatoes, stock, oregano and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer gently for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and rich.
Cook the spaghetti in boiling salted water until al dente, then drain.
Season the sauce, toss with the spaghetti and serve topped with parmesan.

name: Spaghetti carbonara
ingredients: 2 cloves garlic, peeled and left whole
steps: Cook the spaghetti in boiling salted water until al dente, saving a mugful of the water.
Fry the bacon in the oil with the whole garlic cloves until crisp, then discard the garlic.
Beat the eggs, yolks, parmesan and plenty of black pepper in a bowl.
Drain the pasta and tip it into the bacon pan off the heat.
Quickly stir in the egg mixture, loosening with splashes of pasta water until glossy and creamy.
Serve straight away with extra pepper.

name: Tuna pasta bake
steps: Cook the penne in boiling salted water for 2 minutes less than the pack says, then drain.
Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the chopped tomatoes, cream cheese and herbs and stir until smooth.
Mix in the tuna, sweetcorn and pasta, and season well.
Tip into an ovenproof dish and scatter over the cheddar.
Bake at 200C for 20 minutes until bubbling and golden.

name: Chicken and bacon pasta bake
steps: Cook the penne for 2 minutes less than the pack says, then drain.
Fry the chicken, bacon and onion in the oil for 8 minutes until cooked and golden.
Add the garlic, crumbled stock cube and cream and simmer for 3 minutes.
Stir through the pasta and season, then tip into an ovenproof dish.
Scatter over the mozzarella.
Bake at 200C for 20 minutes until bubbling and browned.

name: Pesto pasta
steps: Cook the fusilli in boiling salted water until al dente.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden.
Drain the pasta, keeping a little of the water.
Toss the pasta with the pesto and a splash of the water until coated.
Stir in the tomatoes and season.
Serve topped with parmesan, pine nuts and basil.

name: Sausage pasta
steps: Squeeze the sausage meat from the skins and break it into chunks.
Fry the sausage meat in the oil until browned, about 8 minutes.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes and oregano and simmer for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile cook the penne in boiling salted water, then drain.
Toss the pasta through the sauce, season and top with basil and parmesan.

name: Creamy mushroom pasta
steps: Cook the tagliatelle in boiling salted water, saving a mugful of the water.
Heat the butter and oil in a large pan and fry the mushrooms over a high heat until golden.
Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the cream and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the drained pasta, parmesan and a splash of pasta water and toss together.
Season and scatter with parsley.

name: Pasta arrabbiata
steps: Heat the oil in a pan and gently fry the garlic and chilli flakes for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and sugar and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Cook the penne in boiling salted water until al dente, then drain.
Season the sauce and tear in half the basil.
Toss the pasta through the sauce.
Serve with the remaining basil and parmesan.

name: Pasta puttanesca
steps: Cook the spaghetti in boiling salted water until al dente, then drain.
Heat the oil and stir the garlic and anchovies until the anchovies melt.
Add the chilli flakes and chopped tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the olives and capers.
Toss the spaghetti through the sauce.
Season and finish with parsley.

name: Pasta amatriciana
steps: Fry the bacon in the oil until crisp and the fat has run out.
Add the onion and chilli flakes and cook for 6 minutes until soft.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes.
Cook the spaghetti in boiling salted water until al dente, then drain.
Toss the pasta through the sauce with half the parmesan.
Serve with the rest of the parmesan on top.

name: Cacio e pepe
steps: Cook the spaghetti in a little less water than usual, with salt, until al dente.
Toast the pepper in a dry pan for 1 minute, then add the butter and a ladle of pasta water.
Add the drained spaghetti to the pan and toss over a low heat.
Take off the heat and add the pecorino and parmesan with a splash more pasta water.
Stir hard until the cheese forms a glossy sauce.
Serve immediately with extra pepper.

name: Spaghetti aglio e olio
steps: Cook the spaghetti in boiling salted water until al dente, saving a mugful of the water.
Warm the oil in a large pan over a low heat and add the garlic.
Cook gently for 2 minutes until pale golden, then add the chilli flakes.
Add the spaghetti with a good splash of pasta water and toss over the heat.
Stir in the parsley, season and serve.

name: Prawn linguine
steps: Cook the linguine in boiling salted water until al dente, saving a mugful of the water.
Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the garlic and chilli for 1 minute.
Add the prawns and cook for 2 minutes until just turning pink.
Pour in the wine and add the tomatoes, then simmer for 4 minutes.
Add the drained linguine, lemon juice and a splash of pasta water and toss well.
Season and scatter with parsley.

name: Spaghetti and meatballs
steps: Mix the mince, half the onion, the egg, breadcrumbs, oregano, salt and pepper, then roll into 20 small balls.
Brown the meatballs in half the oil in a large pan, then set aside.
Fry the remaining onion and the garlic in the same pan for 5 minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes and sugar, return the meatballs and simmer for 20 minutes.
Cook the spaghetti in boiling salted water until al dente, then drain.
Serve the meatballs and sauce over the spaghetti.

name: Pasta primavera
steps: Cook the penne in boiling salted water, adding the peas for the final 2 minutes, then drain.
Heat the oil and fry the courgette and asparagus for 5 minutes until just tender.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the cream, lemon zest and juice and simmer for 2 minutes.
Toss in the pasta and peas with the parmesan.
Season well and serve.

name: Tortellini with tomato sauce
steps: Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic.
Add the chopped tomatoes, basil and sugar and simmer for 10 minutes.
Season the sauce well.
Cook the tortellini in boiling water as the pack says, then drain.
Stir the tortellini through the sauce and serve with parmesan.

name: Creamy pesto tortellini
ingredients: 2 x 250g packs fresh spinach and ricotta tortellini
steps: Cook the tortellini in boiling water as the pack says, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes.
Meanwhile warm the pesto and cream in a pan until just bubbling.
Drain the tortellini and peas.
Stir them gently through the creamy pesto.
Season and serve topped with parmesan and rocket.

name: Ravioli with tomato and basil sauce
steps: Warm the oil in a pan and fry the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the chopped tomatoes, tomato puree and sugar and simmer for 10 minutes.
Season and stir in most of the basil.
Cook the ravioli in boiling water as the pack says, then drain.
Toss the ravioli gently through the sauce and serve with parmesan and the rest of the basil.

name: Spinach and ricotta ravioli with sage butter
ingredients: 1 x 250g pack fresh spinach and ricotta ravioli
steps: Cook the ravioli in boiling salted water as the pack says.
Melt the butter in a frying pan until foaming.
Add the sage leaves and garlic and cook for 2 minutes until the sage is crisp.
Lift the drained ravioli into the pan with a splash of the cooking water.
Toss gently, then serve with parmesan and black pepper.

name: Spaghetti with garlic prawns
steps: Cook the spaghetti in boiling salted water until al dente, saving a mugful of the water.
Heat the oil and butter in a large pan and fry the garlic and chilli for 1 minute.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes until pink.
Add the lemon juice and a splash of pasta water.
Toss through the drained spaghetti and parsley, season and serve.

name: Lemon chicken pasta
steps: Cook the linguine in boiling salted water, saving a mugful of the water.
Fry the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the cream, lemon zest and juice and simmer for 3 minutes.
Toss through the drained pasta with the parmesan and a splash of pasta water.
Season and finish with parsley.

name: Chicken alfredo
steps: Cook the fettuccine in boiling salted water until al dente, then drain.
Season the chicken and fry in the oil for 6 minutes until golden and cooked through, then set aside.
Melt the butter in the pan, add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the cream and simmer for 3 minutes, then stir in the parmesan until smooth.
Toss in the pasta and chicken.
Season and top with parsley.

name: Baked ziti
steps: Cook the penne for 2 minutes less than the pack says, then drain.
Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic and mince and brown well.
Add the chopped tomatoes and oregano, then simmer for 15 minutes and season.
Mix the pasta into the sauce along with the ricotta.
Tip into a large dish and top with mozzarella and parmesan.
Bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden and bubbling.

name: Pasta al forno
ingredients: 300g pork sausages, meat removed from skins
steps: Cook the rigatoni for 2 minutes less than the pack says, then drain.
Fry the onion and sausage meat in the oil for 10 minutes until browned.
Add the chopped tomatoes and oregano and simmer for 10 minutes.
Mix the pasta into the sauce with half the mozzarella and season.
Layer into a dish with the egg slices, then top with the rest of the mozzarella and the parmesan.
Bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden.

name: Vegetable lasagne
steps: Fry the onion, courgettes, pepper and mushrooms in the oil for 10 minutes.
Add the garlic, chopped tomatoes and oregano and simmer for 15 minutes, then season.
Spoon a third of the vegetable sauce into a baking dish and top with 3 lasagne sheets.
Add a third of the white sauce, then repeat the layers twice more.
Scatter over the cheddar.
Bake at 190C for 40 minutes until golden and bubbling.

name: Cannelloni
steps: Wilt the spinach in a hot pan, squeeze out the water and chop finely.
Mix the spinach with the ricotta, half the parmesan, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Spoon the filling into the cannelloni tubes using a teaspoon.
Spread the chopped tomatoes and basil over the base of a baking dish and lay the tubes on top.
Cover with white sauce, then scatter over the mozzarella and remaining parmesan.
Bake at 190C for 35 minutes until golden.

name: Lemon and herb orzo
steps: Cook the orzo in boiling salted water for 8 to 10 minutes, then drain.
Return to the pan with the oil and butter.
Stir in the lemon zest and juice.
Add the parsley, basil and parmesan and mix well.
Season and serve warm.

name: One-pot chicken orzo
ingredients: 4 chicken thighs, skinless and boneless, diced
steps: Fry the chicken in the oil in a large pan for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 4 minutes.
Stir in the orzo, chopped tomatoes, stock and oregano.
Simmer for 12 minutes, stirring often, until the orzo is tender.
Stir in the spinach until wilted.
Season and serve.

name: Pasta pomodoro
steps: Warm the oil in a pan and cook the garlic gently for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and sugar and simmer for 15 minutes until thickened.
Cook the spaghetti in boiling salted water until al dente, then drain.
Season the sauce and tear in the basil.
Toss the spaghetti through the sauce and serve with parmesan.

name: Pasta alla norma
steps: Toss the aubergine with 3 tbsp oil and salt, then roast at 200C for 25 minutes until golden.
Fry the onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, then add the garlic.
Add the chopped tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes.
Cook the rigatoni in boiling salted water until al dente, then drain.
Toss the pasta with the sauce and aubergine.
Top with ricotta and basil.

name: Tomato and mascarpone pasta
steps: Cook the penne in boiling salted water until al dente, then drain.
Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the garlic.
Add the chopped tomatoes and tomato puree and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the mascarpone until smooth and season.
Toss through the pasta and top with basil.

name: Chorizo pasta
steps: Cook the penne in boiling salted water until al dente, then drain.
Fry the chorizo in a dry pan for 4 minutes until the oil runs out.
Add the onion and pepper and cook for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, paprika and chopped tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Toss in the pasta, season and scatter with parsley.

name: Chicken and mushroom pasta
steps: Cook the tagliatelle in boiling salted water, then drain, saving a mugful of the water.
Fry the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes until golden, then add the mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the cream and crumbled stock cube and simmer for 3 minutes.
Toss in the pasta with a splash of pasta water.
Season and sprinkle with parsley.

name: Vegetable pasta bake
steps: Cook the fusilli for 2 minutes less than the pack says, then drain.
Fry the onion, courgette and pepper in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, chopped tomatoes and herbs and simmer for 10 minutes.
Mix the pasta into the sauce and season.
Tip into a baking dish and scatter with mozzarella and parmesan.
Bake at 200C for 20 minutes until golden.

name: Sausage pasta bake
steps: Cook the penne for 2 minutes less than the pack says, then drain.
Squeeze the sausage meat out of the skins and brown in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the onion, pepper and garlic and cook for 6 minutes.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes and oregano and simmer for 10 minutes.
Mix in the pasta, season and tip into a baking dish.
Top with cheddar and bake at 200C for 20 minutes.

name: Smoked salmon pasta
steps: Cook the linguine in boiling salted water until al dente, saving a mugful of the water.
Warm the cream, lemon zest and juice in a large pan.
Add the drained pasta and toss with a splash of pasta water.
Take off the heat and fold in the smoked salmon, capers and dill.
Season with black pepper and serve.

name: Salmon and broccoli pasta
ingredients: 1 head broccoli, cut into small florets
steps: Cook the penne in boiling salted water, adding the broccoli for the last 3 minutes, then drain and keep a mugful of the water.
Season the salmon and fry in the oil for 4 minutes each side, then flake into chunks.
Add the garlic to the pan with the cream cheese, lemon zest, juice and a splash of pasta water.
Stir until smooth.
Toss through the pasta, broccoli and salmon.
Season and serve.

name: Ham and pea tagliatelle
steps: Cook the tagliatelle in boiling salted water, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Drain, keeping a mugful of the water.
Melt the butter in the pan, add the cream and simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in the ham and parmesan.
Toss through the pasta and peas, loosening with pasta water.
Season with black pepper.

name: Slow-cooked beef ragu
ingredients: 800g beef shin or braising steak, cut into large chunks
steps: Brown the beef in the oil in a heavy casserole in batches and set aside.
Soften the onion, carrots and celery in the same pan for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and tomato puree.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes.
Return the beef, add the chopped tomatoes and season.
Cover and cook at 160C for 2 and a half hours until the beef falls apart.
Shred the beef into the sauce, cook the pappardelle, toss together and serve with parmesan.

name: Italian pasta salad
steps: Cook the fusilli in boiling salted water until al dente, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Whisk the oil, vinegar and oregano together with salt and pepper.
Tip the pasta into a large bowl.
Add the tomatoes, cucumber, olives, mozzarella and red onion.
Toss with the dressing and top with torn basil.

name: Tuna and sweetcorn pasta salad
steps: Cook the fusilli in boiling salted water, then drain and cool under cold water.
Mix the mayonnaise, yoghurt and lemon juice in a large bowl.
Add the pasta, tuna, sweetcorn, pepper and spring onions.
Stir well and season.
Chill until ready to serve.

name: Courgette and lemon spaghetti
steps: Cook the spaghetti in boiling salted water, saving a mugful of the water.
Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the courgettes for 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute.
Add the drained spaghetti, lemon zest, juice and parmesan.
Toss with a splash of pasta water until creamy.
Season and top with basil.

name: Pasta with broccoli and anchovies
ingredients: 1 head broccoli, cut into small florets
steps: Cook the orecchiette in boiling salted water, adding the broccoli for the last 4 minutes.
Meanwhile warm the oil in a large pan with the anchovies, garlic and chilli flakes until the anchovies dissolve.
Drain the pasta and broccoli, keeping a mugful of the water.
Tip into the pan and mash the broccoli lightly with a spoon.
Toss with parmesan and a splash of pasta water.
Season and serve.

name: Cauliflower pasta bake
steps: Cook the macaroni for 2 minutes less than the pack says, adding the cauliflower for the last 4 minutes, then drain.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk in the milk gradually and simmer until thick.
Stir in the mustard and most of the cheddar and season.
Mix in the pasta and cauliflower and tip into a baking dish.
Top with breadcrumbs and remaining cheddar and bake at 200C for 20 minutes.

name: Creamy leek and ham pasta
steps: Cook the penne in boiling salted water until al dente, saving a mugful of the water.
Melt the butter and fry the leeks for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the cream and mustard and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the ham, pasta and parmesan with a splash of pasta water.
Season and serve.

name: Gorgonzola and spinach pasta
steps: Cook the penne in boiling salted water until al dente, then drain.
Warm the oil and garlic in a pan for 1 minute.
Add the cream and gorgonzola and stir until melted.
Add the spinach and stir until wilted.
Toss through the pasta.
Serve with walnuts and black pepper.

name: Chicken and sun-dried tomato pasta
steps: Cook the penne in boiling salted water until al dente, then drain.
Fry the chicken in the oil for 7 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Add the garlic and sun-dried tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the cream and oregano and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the spinach and parmesan and stir until wilted.
Toss through the pasta and season.

name: Meatball pasta bake
steps: Mix the mince, egg, breadcrumbs, oregano, salt and pepper and roll into 20 balls.
Brown the meatballs in the oil for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, chopped tomatoes and tomato puree and simmer for 10 minutes.
Cook the penne for 2 minutes less than the pack says, then drain.
Mix the pasta into the meatballs and sauce in a baking dish.
Top with mozzarella and bake at 200C for 20 minutes.

name: Tortellini bake
steps: Heat the oven to 200C.
Mix the chopped tomatoes, cream cheese, garlic and basil in a large baking dish.
Stir in the tortellini and spinach and season.
Cover with foil and bake for 15 minutes.
Uncover, scatter over the mozzarella and bake for 10 minutes until golden.

name: Roasted red pepper pasta
steps: Roast the peppers and garlic with the oil at 200C for 25 minutes until soft and charred.
Squeeze the garlic from its skin and blend with the peppers, cream cheese and a splash of water until smooth.
Cook the penne in boiling salted water until al dente, then drain.
Warm the sauce in a pan and season.
Toss through the pasta and serve with basil and parmesan.

name: Crab linguine
steps: Cook the linguine in boiling salted water until al dente, saving a mugful of the water.
Warm the oil in a pan and fry the garlic and chilli for 1 minute.
Add the crab, lemon zest and juice.
Add the drained linguine and a splash of pasta water.
Toss gently, season and stir in the parsley.

name: Stuffed pasta shells
steps: Cook the shells for 2 minutes less than the pack says, then drain.
Mix the ricotta, spinach, half the parmesan, egg, salt and pepper.
Mix the chopped tomatoes, garlic and basil and spread over a baking dish.
Fill each shell with the ricotta mixture and sit them in the sauce.
Top with mozzarella and the rest of the parmesan.
Cover with foil and bake at 190C for 25 minutes, uncovering for the last 10.

name: Spaghetti with tuna and tomato
steps: Cook the spaghetti in boiling salted water until al dente, then drain.
Warm the oil and fry the garlic and chilli flakes for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the tuna and capers and heat through.
Toss through the spaghetti and finish with parsley.

name: Seafood pasta
steps: Cook the linguine in boiling salted water until al dente, then drain.
Fry the garlic in the oil for 1 minute.
Add the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes, then add the chopped tomatoes and chilli flakes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the seafood and cook for 3 minutes until just cooked.
Toss through the linguine with the lemon juice.
Season and scatter with parsley.

name: Gnocchi bake
steps: Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the garlic.
Add the chopped tomatoes and oregano and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the spinach until wilted and season.
Mix in the gnocchi and tip into a baking dish.
Top with mozzarella and bake at 200C for 20 minutes until golden.

name: Gnocchi with pesto
steps: Cook the gnocchi in boiling salted water until they float, about 2 minutes, then drain.
Return to the pan and stir in the pesto and tomatoes.
Heat for 1 minute and season.
Serve topped with rocket and parmesan.

name: Sausage and tomato gnocchi
steps: Squeeze the sausage meat from the skins and fry in the oil, breaking it up, for 8 minutes.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes and oregano and simmer for 10 minutes.
Cook the gnocchi in boiling salted water until they float, then drain.
Stir the gnocchi through the sauce and top with basil and parmesan.

name: Gnocchi with brown butter and sage
steps: Cook the gnocchi in boiling salted water until they float, then drain.
Melt the butter in a large frying pan and cook until it smells nutty and turns golden.
Add the sage leaves and cook for 1 minute until crisp.
Add the gnocchi and fry for 2 minutes until lightly golden.
Serve with parmesan, nutmeg and pepper.

name: Mushroom risotto
steps: Heat the stock in a pan and keep it hot.
Fry the mushrooms in 1 tbsp oil until golden, then set aside.
Soften the onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic and rice and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble away.
Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for about 20 minutes until the rice is creamy and tender.
Stir in the mushrooms, butter and parmesan, season and rest for 2 minutes.

name: Pea and mint risotto
steps: Heat the stock and keep it hot.
Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and rice and stir for 1 minute.
Add the wine and let it bubble away.
Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for about 18 minutes.
Stir in the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Finish with the mint, butter and parmesan and season well.

name: Chicken risotto
steps: Heat the stock and keep it hot.
Fry the chicken in half the oil for 6 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Soften the onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic and rice and stir for 1 minute.
Add the wine, then the stock a ladle at a time for about 20 minutes.
Return the chicken for the last 5 minutes.
Stir in the butter and parmesan and season.

name: Butternut squash risotto
steps: Roast the squash with 1 tbsp oil at 200C for 25 minutes until soft.
Heat the stock and keep it hot.
Soften the onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic and rice and stir for 1 minute.
Add the wine, then the stock a ladle at a time for about 20 minutes.
Stir in the squash, chopped sage and parmesan.
Season and rest for 2 minutes.

name: Prawn risotto
steps: Heat the stock and keep it hot.
Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic and rice and stir for 1 minute.
Add the wine, then the stock a ladle at a time for about 18 minutes.
Add the prawns and peas and cook for 4 minutes until the prawns turn pink.
Stir in the lemon juice and parsley.
Season and serve.

name: Risotto Milanese
steps: Heat the stock, add the saffron and keep it hot.
Melt half the butter and soften the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute, then pour in the wine and let it bubble away.
Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for about 20 minutes until creamy.
Beat in the remaining butter and the parmesan.
Season and rest for 2 minutes before serving.

name: Asparagus risotto
steps: Heat the stock and keep it hot.
Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the rice and stir for 1 minute.
Add the wine, then the stock a ladle at a time for about 18 minutes.
Add the asparagus for the final 4 minutes.
Stir in the lemon zest, butter and parmesan.
Season and serve.

name: Sausage risotto
steps: Heat the stock and keep it hot.
Squeeze the sausage meat from the skins and fry in the oil for 8 minutes until browned.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the rice and thyme.
Add the wine, then the stock a ladle at a time for about 20 minutes.
Stir in the parmesan and season.

name: Tomato risotto
steps: Heat the stock and keep it hot.
Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic and rice and stir for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and oregano and simmer until absorbed.
Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for about 20 minutes.
Stir in the parmesan and season.
Top with torn basil.

name: Margherita pizza
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and put a baking tray in to heat up.
Spread the passata over the base and sprinkle with oregano, salt and pepper.
Scatter over the mozzarella.
Slide onto the hot tray and bake for 10 to 12 minutes until bubbling and golden.
Top with basil and drizzle with oil.

name: Pepperoni pizza
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and put a baking tray in to heat up.
Spread the passata over the base and sprinkle with oregano and pepper.
Scatter over the mozzarella and pepperoni.
Slide onto the hot tray and bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and the edges crisp.

name: Veggie pizza
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and put a baking tray in to heat up.
Spread the passata over the base and sprinkle with oregano.
Scatter over half the mozzarella, then add the vegetables.
Top with the remaining mozzarella and drizzle with oil.
Bake on the hot tray for 12 to 14 minutes until golden.

name: BBQ chicken pizza
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and put a baking tray in to heat up.
Spread the BBQ sauce over the base.
Scatter over half the mozzarella, the chicken, onion and sweetcorn.
Top with the remaining mozzarella.
Bake on the hot tray for 12 minutes until bubbling, then scatter with coriander.

name: Ham and pineapple pizza
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and put a baking tray in to heat up.
Spread the passata over the base and sprinkle with oregano.
Scatter over the mozzarella, ham and pineapple.
Bake on the hot tray for 10 to 12 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Finish with black pepper.

name: Calzone
steps: Mix the flour, yeast and salt, then add the water and oil and knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and leave somewhere warm for 45 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220C and divide the dough in two, rolling each into a 22cm circle.
Spread passata over half of each circle, then top with the mozzarella, ham and basil.
Fold over, press the edges to seal and brush with a little oil.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until golden.

name: Pizza dough
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and sugar in a large bowl.
Add the water and oil and stir to a rough dough.
Knead on a floured surface for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and leave in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 4 balls and roll out each to a thin circle.
Top as you like and bake at 230C for 10 to 12 minutes.

name: Four cheese pizza
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and put a baking tray in to heat up.
Spread the passata over the base.
Scatter over the mozzarella, cheddar and gorgonzola.
Sprinkle with parmesan and oregano and drizzle with oil.
Bake on the hot tray for 10 to 12 minutes until golden.

name: Meat feast pizza
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and put a baking tray in to heat up.
Spread the passata over the base and sprinkle with oregano.
Scatter over half the mozzarella and all the meats.
Top with the rest of the mozzarella.
Bake on the hot tray for 12 minutes until bubbling and golden.

name: French bread pizza
steps: Heat the oven to 200C.
Cut the baguette in half lengthways and then across to make 4 pieces, and lay cut side up on a tray.
Spread with passata and sprinkle with oregano.
Top with the ham, mushrooms and cheddar and drizzle with oil.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the cheese is golden.

name: Pitta bread pizzas
steps: Heat the oven to 200C.
Lay the pittas on a baking tray and spread with tomato puree.
Sprinkle with oregano and add the mozzarella, tomatoes and sweetcorn.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the cheese melts and the edges crisp.
Top with basil.

name: Pizza pinwheels
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and line a baking tray.
Unroll the pastry and spread with the tomato puree, leaving a 1cm border.
Sprinkle with oregano, cheddar and pepperoni.
Roll up tightly from the long side and chill for 10 minutes.
Slice into 12 rounds, lay on the tray and brush with egg.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until puffed and golden.

name: Tuna and sweetcorn pizza
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and put a baking tray in to heat up.
Spread the passata over the base and sprinkle with oregano.
Scatter over half the mozzarella, then the tuna, sweetcorn and onion.
Top with the remaining mozzarella.
Bake on the hot tray for 12 minutes until golden.

name: Garlic bread
steps: Heat the oven to 200C.
Mash the butter with the garlic, parsley and salt.
Cut the baguette diagonally into thick slices without cutting all the way through.
Spread the garlic butter between the slices and over the top.
Wrap in foil and bake for 10 minutes.
Open the foil and bake for 5 minutes more until crisp.

name: Bruschetta
steps: Mix the tomatoes with the basil, oil, vinegar, salt and pepper and leave for 10 minutes.
Toast or grill the ciabatta slices until golden on both sides.
Rub each slice with a cut garlic clove.
Spoon the tomatoes over and serve straight away.

name: Caprese salad
steps: Layer the tomato and mozzarella slices alternately on a platter.
Tuck in the basil leaves.
Drizzle with the oil and balsamic vinegar.
Season well with salt and pepper and serve at room temperature.

name: Panzanella
steps: Toss the bread with half the oil and bake at 200C for 10 minutes until crisp.
Mix the tomatoes, cucumber and onion in a large bowl with salt.
Whisk the remaining oil with the vinegar and pepper and pour over.
Add the bread and basil and toss.
Leave for 10 minutes to soak before serving.

name: Arancini
steps: Mix the cold risotto with the parmesan and season.
Take a spoonful, press a mozzarella cube into the middle and roll into a ball, making 12.
Roll each ball in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 180C.
Fry in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until golden, then drain on kitchen paper.

name: Focaccia
steps: Mix the flour, yeast and salt, then stir in the water and 2 tbsp oil to a sticky dough.
Cover and leave for 1 hour until doubled.
Tip into an oiled 30 x 20cm tin, stretching it to fit, and leave for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220C and dimple the dough with oiled fingers.
Drizzle with the remaining oil and top with rosemary and sea salt.
Bake for 25 minutes until golden.

name: Mozzarella sticks
steps: Freeze the mozzarella sticks for 30 minutes so they hold their shape.
Season the flour, and mix the oregano into the breadcrumbs.
Coat each stick in flour, egg, then breadcrumbs, and repeat the egg and crumbs for a double coat.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 180C.
Fry for 1 to 2 minutes until golden and drain on kitchen paper.

name: Garlic flatbreads
steps: Mix the flour, yoghurt and salt into a dough and knead briefly.
Divide into 4 and roll each into an oval about 5mm thick.
Cook in a hot dry frying pan for 2 minutes each side until puffed and spotted.
Mix the melted butter with the garlic and parsley.
Brush over the hot flatbreads and serve.

name: Rocket and parmesan salad
steps: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden.
Put the rocket in a bowl.
Whisk the oil and balsamic vinegar with salt and pepper and toss through.
Top with parmesan shavings and pine nuts and serve.

name: Chicken parmigiana
steps: Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally, or flatten with a rolling pin, and season.
Coat in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs mixed with the parmesan.
Fry in the oil for 3 minutes each side until golden and place in a baking dish.
Simmer the garlic, chopped tomatoes and oregano for 10 minutes and season.
Spoon the sauce over the chicken and top with mozzarella.
Bake at 200C for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the cheese is golden.

name: Pork milanese
steps: Bash the pork steaks between sheets of cling film until about 1cm thick and season.
Coat in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs mixed with the parmesan.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan.
Fry the pork for 3 to 4 minutes each side until golden and cooked through.
Drain on kitchen paper.
Serve with rocket and lemon wedges.

name: Chicken cacciatore
steps: Season the chicken and brown in the oil in a large casserole, skin side down first, then set aside.
Fry the onion and pepper in the same pan for 6 minutes, then add the garlic.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes, olives and oregano and return the chicken.
Cover and simmer gently for 35 minutes until tender.
Season and scatter with parsley.

name: Osso buco
steps: Season the beef and dust with flour.
Brown in the oil in a casserole for 3 minutes each side and set aside.
Soften the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes, then add the garlic.
Add the wine, chopped tomatoes and stock and return the beef.
Cover and cook at 160C for 2 hours until the meat is very tender.
Mix the lemon zest and parsley and sprinkle over to serve.

name: Italian meatloaf
steps: Heat the oven to 190C and line a loaf tin or tray.
Mix the mince, onion, garlic, egg, breadcrumbs, parmesan, oregano, basil, salt and pepper.
Shape into a loaf in the tin and spoon over half the chopped tomatoes.
Bake for 45 minutes.
Top with mozzarella and the remaining tomatoes and bake for 15 minutes more.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

name: Chicken saltimbocca
steps: Slice the chicken breasts in half horizontally and flatten to 1cm thick, then season.
Lay a sage leaf and a slice of Parma ham on each piece and secure with a cocktail stick.
Dust lightly with flour.
Fry in the oil, ham side down first, for 3 minutes each side and set aside.
Pour the wine and stock into the pan and boil for 3 minutes, then whisk in the butter.
Return the chicken to the sauce and serve.

name: Sausage and white bean stew
steps: Brown the sausages in the oil in a large pan, then cut each into chunks.
Add the onion and carrots to the pan and cook for 8 minutes, then add the garlic.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes, beans, stock and rosemary and return the sausages.
Simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the kale for the last 5 minutes and season to serve.

name: Creamy polenta with mushrooms
steps: Bring the stock to the boil and pour in the polenta in a steady stream, whisking.
Cook on a low heat for 10 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Beat in the butter and parmesan and season.
Fry the mushrooms in the oil over a high heat for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute.
Spoon the polenta into bowls and top with the mushrooms.

name: Aubergine parmigiana
steps: Brush the aubergine slices with 3 tbsp oil and roast at 200C for 20 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Fry the onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and oregano and simmer for 15 minutes, then season.
Layer the sauce, aubergine, mozzarella, basil and parmesan in a baking dish, finishing with cheese.
Bake at 190C for 25 minutes until golden and bubbling.

name: Italian chicken traybake
steps: Heat the oven to 200C.
Tip the potatoes, pepper, onion, tomatoes and garlic into a large roasting tin.
Add the chicken, oil, oregano, salt and pepper and toss well, leaving the chicken skin side up.
Roast for 40 minutes.
Add the olives and roast for 10 minutes more until the chicken is golden and cooked through.

name: Steak pizzaiola
steps: Season the steaks and fry in 1 tbsp oil for 2 to 3 minutes each side, then set aside to rest.
Add the remaining oil and the garlic to the pan and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the chopped tomatoes, oregano and capers and simmer for 10 minutes.
Season and return the steaks with any juices for 1 minute.
Serve with the sauce spooned over and topped with basil.

name: Sausage and pepper traybake
steps: Heat the oven to 200C.
Put the sausages, peppers, onions and garlic in a large roasting tin.
Add the oil, oregano, salt and pepper and toss together.
Roast for 35 minutes, turning once.
Drizzle with balsamic vinegar and roast for 10 minutes more until sticky.

name: Italian meatballs in tomato sauce
steps: Mix the mince, egg, breadcrumbs, parmesan, oregano, salt and pepper and roll into 20 balls.
Brown the meatballs in half the oil and set aside.
Fry the onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, then add the garlic.
Add the chopped tomatoes and simmer for 5 minutes.
Return the meatballs and cook gently for 20 minutes.
Season and top with torn basil.

name: Creamy Tuscan chicken
steps: Season the chicken and fry in the oil for 6 minutes each side until golden and cooked through, then set aside.
Add the garlic and sun-dried tomatoes to the pan and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the cream, stock and herbs and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the parmesan and spinach until wilted.
Return the chicken and spoon the sauce over.

name: Courgette and parmesan frittata
steps: Heat the oil in an ovenproof frying pan and fry the onion and courgettes for 8 minutes until golden.
Beat the eggs with the parmesan, basil, salt and pepper.
Pour the eggs over the vegetables and cook over a low heat for 5 minutes until the edges set.
Place under a hot grill for 3 to 4 minutes until the top is golden and set.
Cut into wedges and serve warm or cold.

name: Spaghetti frittata
steps: Beat the eggs with the parmesan, parsley, salt and pepper.
Stir in the cooked spaghetti and peas.
Heat the oil in an ovenproof frying pan and pour in the mixture.
Cook over a low heat for 6 minutes until the base is set.
Grill for 3 to 4 minutes until golden on top.
Cut into wedges to serve.

name: Meatball sub
steps: Mix the mince, egg, breadcrumbs, oregano, salt and pepper and roll into 16 balls.
Brown the meatballs in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and chopped tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes.
Split the rolls and fill with meatballs and sauce.
Top with mozzarella and grill for 3 minutes until melted.

name: Pesto chicken
steps: Heat the oven to 200C.
Slash each chicken breast a few times and put in a baking dish.
Spread the pesto over the chicken, season and add the tomatoes and oil around it.
Bake for 20 minutes.
Top with mozzarella and bake for 8 minutes more until the chicken is cooked through.
Scatter with basil.

name: Chicken and broccoli pasta
