Roll out the remaining pastry for a lid, seal the edges and cut a slit in the top. Brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until golden. Serve warm with cream or custard.

name: Bread and butter pudding
steps: Heat the oven to 180C. Butter the bread, cut it into triangles and layer in a baking dish with the sultanas.
Warm the milk and cream, then whisk with the eggs, caster sugar and vanilla.
Pour the custard over the bread and leave to soak for 15 minutes. Sprinkle with demerara sugar.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until set and golden on top.

name: Treacle tart
steps: Rub the butter into the flour and bring together with the water to make pastry. Chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 190C. Roll out the pastry and line a 23cm tart tin, then blind bake for 15 minutes with baking paper and beans.
Warm the golden syrup and stir in the breadcrumbs, the juice and zest of the lemon and the egg.
Pour the filling into the pastry case and bake for 25 minutes until just set and golden. Serve warm.

name: Treacle sponge pudding
steps: Grease a 1.2 litre pudding basin and spoon the golden syrup into the bottom.
Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs a little at a time. Fold in the flour, the lemon zest and the milk.
Spoon the mixture over the syrup and cover with pleated foil tied with string.
Steam in a pan of simmering water for 2 hours, topping up the water as needed.
Turn out onto a plate and serve with custard.

name: Jam roly-poly
steps: Heat the oven to 180C. Mix the flour, suet and salt, then stir in enough water to form a soft dough.
Roll out into a 25 x 30cm rectangle and spread with jam, leaving a 2cm border.
Brush the edges with milk, roll up from the short side and seal the ends.
Wrap loosely in baking paper and foil and bake for 40 minutes. Slice and serve with custard.

name: Spotted dick
steps: Mix the flour, suet, sugar, currants, salt and lemon zest in a bowl.
Stir in enough milk to make a soft dough and shape into a roll about 15cm long.
Wrap in baking paper and then foil, leaving room to expand, and tie the ends.
Steam over simmering water for 1 hour 45 minutes. Slice and serve with custard.

name: Eve's pudding
steps: Heat the oven to 180C. Put the apples, the first measure of sugar and the cloves in a baking dish with 2 tbsp water.
Beat the butter and second measure of sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs.
Fold in the flour and milk, then spread the sponge mixture over the apples.
Bake for 40 minutes until the sponge is golden and springy. Serve with custard.

name: Eton mess
steps: Crush half the strawberries with the sugar and slice the rest.
Whip the cream with the vanilla until it just holds soft peaks.
Gently fold the meringue, sliced strawberries and crushed strawberries through the cream.
Spoon into glasses and serve straight away.

name: Sherry trifle
steps: Split the sponges, sandwich with jam and arrange in the bottom of a large glass bowl.
Drizzle over the sherry and scatter with the fruit.
Pour over the cooled custard and chill for at least 2 hours.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar and spread over the custard.
Top with toasted flaked almonds just before serving.

name: Rice pudding
steps: Heat the oven to 150C. Put the rice, sugar, milk, cream and vanilla in a buttered baking dish and stir.
Dot the butter on top and grate over the nutmeg.
Bake for 2 hours, stirring once after 30 minutes, until creamy with a golden skin.
Serve hot with a spoonful of jam.

name: Custard
steps: Heat the milk, cream and vanilla in a pan until steaming but not boiling.
Whisk the egg yolks, sugar and cornflour together in a bowl until smooth.
Slowly pour the hot milk over the yolks, whisking constantly, then return to the pan.
Stir over a low heat for 5 to 8 minutes until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

name: Chocolate sponge pudding
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and grease a 1.5 litre baking dish.
Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Fold in the flour and cocoa with the milk, then spoon into the dish.
Bake for 30 minutes until risen and springy.
Warm the cream, pour over the chocolate and stir until glossy. Serve the sauce with the sponge.

name: Syrup sponge pudding
steps: Grease 6 microwave-safe pudding basins or one large basin and spoon syrup into the base.
Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs, flour, milk and lemon zest.
Spoon the mixture over the syrup and cover loosely with cling film, leaving a vent.
Microwave on high for 4 to 5 minutes for a large pudding, or 90 seconds for small ones, until risen and cooked through.
Turn out and serve with custard.

name: Bakewell tart
steps: Rub the cold butter into the flour, add the yolk and water and bring to a dough. Chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 190C. Line a 23cm tart tin with the pastry and blind bake for 15 minutes.
Spread the jam over the base. Beat the softened butter and sugar, then beat in the eggs and fold in the ground almonds.
Spoon over the jam, scatter with flaked almonds and bake for 30 minutes until golden and set.

name: Lemon tart
steps: Rub the butter into the flour and icing sugar, then add the yolk and water to make a dough. Chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180C. Line a 23cm tart tin and blind bake for 15 minutes, then 5 minutes without the beans.
Whisk the eggs and sugar, then stir in the zest and juice of the lemons and the cream.
Pour the filling into the case and bake for 30 minutes until just set with a slight wobble. Cool before slicing.

name: Pavlova
steps: Heat the oven to 150C and draw a 20cm circle on baking paper on a tray.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, then whisk in the sugar a spoonful at a time until thick and glossy. Fold in the cornflour and vinegar.
Pile onto the circle, make a dip in the middle and bake for 1 hour. Turn off the oven and leave to cool inside.
Whip the cream, spoon onto the meringue and top with the berries.

name: Banoffee pie
steps: Crush the biscuits and mix with the melted butter. Press into a 23cm tin and chill for 30 minutes.
Spread the caramel over the base.
Slice the bananas and arrange over the caramel.
Whip the cream to soft peaks, spoon on top and finish with grated chocolate.

name: Baked vanilla cheesecake
steps: Heat the oven to 160C. Crush the biscuits, mix with the butter and press into a 23cm springform tin.
Beat the cream cheese, sugar and flour until smooth, then beat in the eggs, vanilla and soured cream.
Pour over the base and bake for 50 minutes until set with a slight wobble.
Turn off the oven and leave the cheesecake inside with the door ajar for 1 hour, then chill overnight.

name: No-bake strawberry cheesecake
steps: Crush the biscuits, mix with the butter and press into a 20cm springform tin. Chill.
Beat the cream cheese, icing sugar and vanilla until smooth. Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold in.
Spoon over the base, smooth the top and chill for at least 4 hours.
Warm the jam, arrange the strawberries on top and brush with the jam to glaze.

name: Chocolate mousse
steps: Melt the chocolate in a bowl over a pan of simmering water, then leave to cool slightly.
Stir the egg yolks into the chocolate one at a time.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold into the chocolate.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks with the sugar, then fold in gently. Spoon into glasses and chill for 3 hours.

name: Lemon posset
steps: Gently heat the cream and sugar in a pan, stirring until the sugar dissolves, then boil for 3 minutes.
Take off the heat and stir in the juice of the lemons and the zest of one.
Strain into 6 small glasses and cool.
Chill for at least 3 hours until set and serve topped with raspberries.

name: Panna cotta
steps: Soak the gelatine leaves in cold water for 5 minutes.
Heat the milk, cream, sugar and vanilla until just steaming, then take off the heat.
Squeeze out the gelatine and stir into the hot cream until dissolved.
Pour into 6 moulds and chill for 4 hours. Turn out and serve with the strawberries.

name: Tiramisu
steps: Whisk the egg yolks and sugar until pale, then beat in the mascarpone.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold into the mascarpone mixture.
Mix the coffee and liqueur, quickly dip the sponge fingers and layer in a dish.
Spread over half the cream, repeat the layers and chill for 4 hours. Dust with cocoa before serving.

name: Creme brulee
steps: Heat the oven to 150C. Warm the cream with the split vanilla pod until steaming.
Whisk the egg yolks and the 75g sugar until pale, then pour in the cream, whisking, and strain.
Divide between 6 ramekins in a roasting tin, pour hot water halfway up the sides and bake for 35 minutes until just set.
Cool and chill for at least 4 hours. Sprinkle each with 1 tbsp sugar and caramelise with a blowtorch or under a hot grill.

name: Profiteroles
steps: Heat the oven to 200C. Melt the butter in the water, bring to the boil, then tip in the flour and beat to a smooth paste. Cool for 5 minutes.
Beat in the eggs a little at a time until you have a glossy, dropping paste.
Pipe or spoon 18 small balls onto lined trays and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden. Pierce each and cool on a rack.
Whip the 300ml cream with the icing sugar and fill the buns.
Melt the chocolate with the 100ml cream, pour over the profiteroles and serve.

name: Chocolate fondant
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and butter and flour 4 ramekins.
Melt the chocolate and butter together and leave to cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs, yolks and sugar until thick, then fold in the chocolate and flour.
Divide between the ramekins and bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the tops are set but the middles wobble. Turn out and serve at once.

name: Baked apples
steps: Heat the oven to 180C. Core the apples and score a line around the middle of each.
Mix the sultanas, sugar and cinnamon and stuff into the apple cavities.
Stand in a baking dish, top each with butter and pour the apple juice around them.
Bake for 40 minutes until soft. Serve with custard.

name: Poached pears
steps: Put the wine, sugar, cinnamon, cloves and strips of orange peel in a pan and heat until the sugar dissolves.
Add the pears, cover and simmer gently for 20 to 25 minutes until tender.
Lift out the pears and boil the liquid for 10 minutes until syrupy.
Serve the pears with the syrup spooned over, with cream or ice cream.

name: Summer pudding
steps: Heat the berries, sugar and water gently for 3 minutes until the juices run. Do not overcook.
Line a 1 litre pudding basin with cling film, then line with bread, cutting pieces to fit with no gaps.
Spoon in the fruit, reserving some juice, and cover the top with bread.
Put a plate with a weight on top and chill overnight.
Turn out and serve with the reserved juice and cream.

name: Knickerbocker glory
steps: Layer strawberries and raspberry sauce in the bottom of 4 tall glasses.
Add alternate scoops of vanilla and strawberry ice cream.
Whip the cream and spoon a swirl on top.
Finish with chopped nuts, more sauce and a wafer.

name: Arctic roll
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and line a 23 x 33cm Swiss roll tin. Whisk the eggs and sugar for 5 minutes until thick and pale.
Fold in the flour and water, pour into the tin and bake for 10 minutes.
Turn out onto sugared baking paper, roll up and leave to cool. Unroll and spread with jam.
Spread the ice cream over the sponge, roll up tightly and wrap. Freeze for 3 hours, then slice.

name: Bread pudding
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line a 20cm square tin. Tear the bread into a bowl and pour over the milk. Leave to soak for 15 minutes.
Mash the bread with a fork, then stir in the butter, brown sugar, dried fruit, mixed spice, egg and orange zest.
Spoon into the tin, level the top and sprinkle with demerara sugar.
Bake for 1 hour until firm and golden. Cool and cut into squares.

name: Christmas pudding
steps: Mix the dried fruit with the brandy, stout and orange juice and zest and soak overnight.
Stir in the sugar, suet, breadcrumbs, flour, spice, apple and eggs.
Spoon into a greased 1.5 litre pudding basin, cover with pleated baking paper and foil and tie with string.
Steam for 6 hours, topping up the water, then cool and store. On the day, steam for another 2 hours and serve with brandy butter.

name: Mince pies
steps: Rub the butter into the flour and icing sugar, add the yolk and water and bring to a dough. Chill for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200C. Roll out the pastry and cut 12 circles and 12 smaller lids or stars.
Line a 12-hole tin with the larger circles, fill with mincemeat and top with the lids.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 15 to 18 minutes until golden.

name: Yule log
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and line a 23 x 33cm Swiss roll tin. Whisk the eggs and caster sugar until thick, then fold in the flour and cocoa.
Bake for 10 minutes, turn out onto sugared paper, roll up with the paper and cool.
Whip the cream with 2 tbsp icing sugar, unroll the sponge and spread with the cream, then re-roll.
Melt the chocolate, cool slightly and beat with the butter and 100g icing sugar to make icing.
Cover the log with the icing and drag a fork along it to mimic bark. Dust with icing sugar.

name: Christmas cake
steps: Soak the dried fruit in the brandy overnight. Heat the oven to 140C and line a 20cm deep round tin.
Beat the butter and sugar until fluffy, then beat in the eggs, treacle and zest of the orange.
Fold in the flour, spice, soaked fruit, cherries and almonds.
Spoon into the tin, level and bake for 3 hours until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin, then wrap and feed with a little more brandy weekly until Christmas.

name: Apple strudel
steps: Heat the oven to 190C. Toss the apples with the sultanas, sugar, cinnamon and lemon zest and juice.
Fry the breadcrumbs in 25g of the butter until golden.
Layer the filo sheets on a tray, brushing each with butter, and scatter over the crumbs.
Spoon the apple along one long edge, roll up and brush with butter.
Bake for 35 minutes until golden. Dust with icing sugar and serve warm.

name: Pancakes with lemon and sugar
steps: Whisk the flour, salt, eggs and milk into a smooth batter, then stir in the melted butter. Rest for 15 minutes.
Heat a little oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat.
Pour in a thin layer of batter, tilting the pan, and cook for 1 minute each side until golden.
Sprinkle with sugar and a squeeze of lemon, then roll up and serve.

name: Crepes suzette
steps: Whisk the flour, eggs and milk into a batter, add the melted butter and rest for 15 minutes. Cook 8 thin pancakes and keep warm.
Melt the 50g butter and sugar in a wide pan until it begins to caramelise.
Add the juice and zest of the oranges and simmer for 3 minutes.
Fold each pancake into quarters and warm in the sauce. Add the liqueur and spoon the sauce over to serve.

name: Baklava
steps: Heat the oven to 180C. Mix the nuts with the cinnamon.
Brush a 20cm square tin with butter and layer in half the filo, brushing each sheet with butter. Add the nuts, then the rest of the filo.
Cut into diamonds with a sharp knife and bake for 35 minutes until golden.
Simmer the sugar, water, honey and lemon juice for 10 minutes, then pour the cooled syrup over the hot baklava. Leave to soak.

name: Sticky ginger pudding
steps: Heat the oven to 160C and grease a 20cm square tin.
Melt the butter, sugar, syrup and treacle in a pan and cool slightly.
Whisk in the egg and milk, then stir into the flour, ginger and bicarbonate of soda until smooth. Stir in the stem ginger.
Pour into the tin and bake for 45 minutes until risen and sticky. Serve warm with custard.

name: Queen of puddings
steps: Heat the oven to 160C. Warm the milk with the butter and lemon zest, then pour over the breadcrumbs.
Stir in the egg yolks and 25g of the sugar. Pour into a baking dish and bake for 25 minutes until set.
Warm the jam and spread it over the top.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, whisk in the remaining sugar, and pile over the jam. Bake for 15 minutes until golden.

name: Blancmange
steps: Mix a little of the milk with the cornflour to make a smooth paste.
Heat the remaining milk with the sugar until nearly boiling, then stir in the paste and cook, whisking, until thick.
Stir in the vanilla and cream and pour into 6 wetted moulds.
Chill for 3 hours until set, turn out and serve with raspberries.

name: Semolina pudding
steps: Heat the milk in a pan until almost boiling.
Sprinkle in the semolina, whisking, and add the sugar.
Simmer for 5 to 8 minutes, stirring, until thick. Stir in the vanilla.
Serve in bowls with a spoonful of jam and a little grated nutmeg.

name: Rhubarb fool
steps: Put the rhubarb, sugar and the juice of the orange in a pan and simmer for 10 minutes until soft. Cool completely.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold in the custard.
Swirl the rhubarb through the cream, leaving some ripples.
Spoon into glasses and chill for 1 hour.

name: Gooseberry fool
steps: Simmer the gooseberries with the sugar and water for 10 minutes until they burst. Mash and leave to cool.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold in the custard.
Fold the gooseberry puree through, leaving some streaks.
Spoon into glasses and chill for 1 hour.

name: Chocolate brownies
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line a 20cm square tin.
Melt the chocolate and butter together, then leave to cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk in the sugar and eggs, then fold in the flour, cocoa, salt and chocolate chips.
Pour into the tin and bake for 25 minutes until the top is crusty but the middle is still fudgy. Cool before cutting.

name: Blondies
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line a 20cm square tin.
Beat the melted butter and sugar together, then beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Fold in the flour, baking powder, salt and chocolate chips.
Spread into the tin and bake for 25 minutes until golden with a slight wobble in the middle. Cool and cut into squares.

name: Millionaire's shortbread
steps: Heat the oven to 180C. Rub the first measure of butter into the flour and caster sugar, press into a lined 20cm tin and bake for 20 minutes until golden.
Melt the second measure of butter with the brown sugar, condensed milk and golden syrup over a low heat.
Bring to a gentle boil and stir for 6 to 8 minutes until thick and golden. Pour over the shortbread and cool.
Melt the chocolate, spread over the caramel and chill until set. Cut into squares.

name: Flapjacks
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line a 20cm square tin.
Melt the butter, sugar and golden syrup in a pan, then stir in the oats and salt.
Press into the tin and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden at the edges.
Mark into squares while warm and cut when completely cool.

name: Rocky road
steps: Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Melt the chocolate, butter and golden syrup together over a low heat, then cool slightly.
Stir in the biscuits, marshmallows and cherries until coated.
Press into the tin and chill for 2 hours. Cut into squares.

name: Chocolate tiffin
steps: Line a 20cm square tin.
Melt the butter, golden syrup and cocoa in a pan, then stir in the biscuits and raisins.
Press into the tin and chill for 30 minutes.
Melt the chocolate, spread over the top and chill for 2 hours before cutting.

name: Rice Krispie cakes
steps: Melt the chocolate, butter and golden syrup together in a pan over a low heat.
Take off the heat and stir in the rice krispies until coated.
Spoon into the cake cases.
Chill for 1 hour until set.

name: Victoria sponge
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and grease and line two 20cm sandwich tins.
Beat the butter and sugar until pale and fluffy, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Fold in the flour and baking powder with the milk, then divide between the tins and bake for 22 minutes until golden.
Cool, then spread one cake with jam and whipped cream and sandwich together. Dust with icing sugar.

name: Lemon drizzle cake
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line a 900g loaf tin.
Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs. Fold in the flour, milk and zest of the 2 lemons.
Spoon into the tin and bake for 45 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Mix the juice of the lemons with the icing sugar, prick the warm cake all over and pour over the drizzle. Cool in the tin.

name: Carrot cake
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line a 20cm square tin.
Whisk the oil, sugar and eggs together, then fold in the flour, spice, carrots and walnuts.
Pour into the tin and bake for 40 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat the cream cheese, butter and icing sugar until smooth, spread over the cake and cut into squares.

name: Coffee and walnut cake
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line two 20cm sandwich tins. Dissolve the first measure of coffee in 2 tbsp hot water.
Beat the butter and sugar until fluffy, beat in the eggs, then fold in the flour, coffee and half the walnuts.
Bake for 25 minutes until risen and golden. Cool.
Beat the remaining butter, icing sugar and second measure of coffee dissolved in 1 tbsp hot water. Sandwich and top the cake and decorate with the remaining walnuts.

name: Chocolate cake
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line two 20cm sandwich tins.
Beat the butter and sugar until fluffy, then beat in the eggs. Fold in the flour, cocoa, baking powder and milk.
Divide between the tins and bake for 25 minutes until risen. Cool on a rack.
Heat the cream until steaming, pour over the chopped chocolate and stir until smooth. Cool until thick, then sandwich and cover the cake.

name: Chocolate fudge cake
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line two 20cm sandwich tins.
Beat the butter and sugar until fluffy, beat in the eggs, then fold in the flour, first measure of cocoa and the soured cream.
Divide between the tins and bake for 25 minutes. Cool completely.
Melt the 100g butter with the milk, stir in the icing sugar and remaining cocoa and beat until thick and fudgy.
Sandwich the cakes and cover the top and sides with the icing.

name: Red velvet cake
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line two 20cm sandwich tins.
Beat the first measure of butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs, buttermilk and colouring.
Fold in the flour, cocoa and bicarbonate of soda, then stir in the vinegar. Divide between the tins and bake for 25 minutes. Cool.
Beat the cream cheese, remaining butter and icing sugar until smooth. Sandwich and cover the cake.

name: Banana bread
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line a 900g loaf tin.
Mash the bananas and mix with the melted butter, sugar and eggs.
Fold in the flour, bicarbonate of soda, baking powder, cinnamon and walnuts.
Pour into the tin and bake for 55 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool on a rack.

name: Ginger cake
steps: Heat the oven to 160C and line a 20cm square tin.
Melt the butter, sugar, syrup and treacle together and leave to cool slightly.
Whisk in the eggs and milk, then stir into the flour, spices and bicarbonate of soda until smooth.
Pour into the tin and bake for 45 minutes until firm. Keep for a day or two for a stickier cake.

name: Fruit cake
steps: Heat the oven to 150C and line a 20cm round tin.
Beat the butter and sugar until fluffy, then beat in the eggs a little at a time with a spoonful of flour.
Fold in the flour, spice, dried fruit, cherries, orange zest and milk.
Spoon into the tin and bake for 2 hours 15 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin.

name: Dundee cake
steps: Heat the oven to 150C and line a 20cm round tin.
Beat the butter, sugar and orange zest until pale, then beat in the eggs.
Fold in the flour, baking powder, ground almonds, dried fruit and milk.
Spoon into the tin, level and arrange the whole almonds in circles on top.
Bake for 2 hours 15 minutes until golden and firm. Cool in the tin.

name: Battenberg
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line a 20cm square tin with a foil divider down the middle.
Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs. Fold in the flour, ground almonds and almond extract.
Colour half the mixture pink, spoon both halves into the tin and bake for 30 minutes. Cool.
Trim and cut into four long strips. Stick together in a checkerboard with warmed jam.
Roll the marzipan on icing sugar, brush with jam, wrap round the cake and trim the ends.

name: Swiss roll
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and line a 23 x 33cm Swiss roll tin.
Whisk the eggs and 100g sugar for 5 minutes until thick and pale. Fold in the flour and hot water.
Pour into the tin and bake for 10 minutes until golden.
Turn out onto sugared baking paper, roll up with the paper inside and cool. Unroll, spread with jam and roll again.

name: Madeira cake
steps: Heat the oven to 160C and line a 900g loaf tin.
Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs and lemon zest.
Fold in both flours and the milk and spoon into the tin. Lay the citron peel on top.
Bake for 1 hour until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool on a rack.

name: Marble cake
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line a 900g loaf tin.
Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs and vanilla. Fold in the flour and 2 tbsp milk.
Take out a third of the mixture and stir in the cocoa and remaining milk.
Spoon alternating blobs of the plain and chocolate batter into the tin and swirl with a skewer.
Bake for 50 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.

name: Cupcakes
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line a 12-hole muffin tin with cases.
Beat the first measure of butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs, flour, milk and vanilla.
Divide between the cases and bake for 18 minutes until golden. Cool.
Beat the remaining butter and icing sugar with the milk until fluffy and pipe or spread onto the cakes.

name: Butterfly cakes
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line a 12-hole bun tin with cases.
Beat the first measure of butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs, flour and milk.
Divide between the cases and bake for 15 minutes. Cool.
Beat the remaining butter and icing sugar for the buttercream. Cut a circle from the top of each cake and halve it to make wings.
Fill with jam and buttercream and press the wings on top. Dust with icing sugar.

name: Chocolate muffins
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and line a 12-hole muffin tin with cases.
Mix the flour, cocoa, baking powder and sugar in a bowl.
Whisk the eggs, milk and oil together and pour into the dry ingredients with the chocolate chips. Stir briefly until just combined.
Divide between the cases and bake for 20 minutes until risen.

name: Blueberry muffins
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and line a 12-hole muffin tin with cases.
Mix the flour, baking powder and sugar in a bowl.
Whisk the eggs, milk, melted butter and vanilla and pour into the dry mix. Add the blueberries and stir briefly.
Divide between the cases and bake for 20 to 22 minutes until golden and risen.

name: Scones
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and put a baking tray in to warm.
Rub the butter into the flour and baking powder, then stir in the sugar.
Mix in the milk to make a soft dough, pat out to 3cm thick and cut into rounds with a 6cm cutter.
Place on the hot tray, brush the tops with egg and bake for 12 minutes until risen and golden. Serve with jam and cream.

name: Welsh cakes
steps: Rub the butter into the flour and mixed spice, then stir in the sugar and currants.
Add the egg and milk and bring to a firm dough.
Roll out to 5mm thick and cut into rounds with a 6cm cutter.
Cook on a medium heat on a lightly greased griddle or frying pan for 3 minutes each side until golden. Dust with sugar.

name: Rock cakes
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and line a baking tray.
Rub the butter into the flour and spice, then stir in the sugar and sultanas.
Mix in the egg and milk to make a stiff dough.
Spoon 12 rough heaps onto the tray and bake for 15 minutes until golden.

name: Eccles cakes
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and line a tray. Mix the butter, currants, brown sugar, spice and orange zest.
Roll out the pastry and cut 12 circles about 9cm across.
Put a spoonful of filling in the middle of each, gather the edges and pinch to seal. Turn over and flatten gently with a rolling pin.
Slash the tops three times, brush with egg white, sprinkle with caster sugar and bake for 20 minutes until golden.

name: Chelsea buns
steps: Warm the milk with the first measure of butter and mix with the flour, yeast, caster sugar, salt and egg. Knead for 10 minutes and leave to rise for 1 hour.
Roll the dough into a 30 x 40cm rectangle. Spread with the softened butter and scatter with currants, brown sugar and spice.
Roll up from the long side, cut into 12 slices and place in a lined tin. Cover and prove for 45 minutes.
Heat the oven to 190C and bake for 25 minutes until golden. Warm the jam and brush over the buns.

name: Hot cross buns
steps: Mix the bread flour, yeast, sugar, salt and spice. Add the warm milk, butter and egg and knead for 10 minutes.
Knead in the sultanas and orange zest, cover and leave to rise for 1 hour.
Divide into 12 balls, place in a lined tin and prove for 45 minutes.
Mix the plain flour with about 5 tbsp water to a paste and pipe crosses on the buns.
Bake at 200C for 20 minutes. Warm the jam and brush over the hot buns.

name: Bakewell slices
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line a 20 x 30cm tin. Rub the cold butter into the flour, add the yolk and water to bring to a dough.
Press the pastry into the tin and prick with a fork. Bake for 15 minutes.
Spread with the jam. Beat the soft butter and sugar, then beat in the eggs and fold in the ground almonds.
Spread over the jam, scatter with flaked almonds and bake for 30 minutes until golden. Cool and cut into slices.

name: Parkin
steps: Heat the oven to 150C and line a 20cm square tin.
Mix the flour, oatmeal, ginger, spice and bicarbonate of soda.
Melt the butter, sugar, treacle and syrup together and cool slightly. Beat in the egg and milk.
Stir into the dry mix, pour into the tin and bake for 1 hour until firm. Store for a few days before cutting for a stickier parkin.

name: Bara brith
steps: Soak the dried fruit and sugar in the hot tea overnight.
Heat the oven to 160C and line a 900g loaf tin.
Stir the egg, flour and spice into the soaked fruit until combined.
Pour into the tin and bake for 1 hour 15 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Serve sliced and buttered.

name: Malt loaf
steps: Soak the dried fruit in the hot tea for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 150C and line a 900g loaf tin.
Warm the malt extract, treacle and sugar until melted and stir into the fruit.
Add the egg and flour and mix well.
Pour into the tin and bake for 1 hour until firm. Cool and serve sliced and buttered.

name: Date and walnut loaf
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line a 900g loaf tin.
Pour the boiling water over the dates with the bicarbonate of soda and butter and stir until the butter melts.
Stir in the sugar and egg, then fold in the flour and walnuts.
Pour into the tin and bake for 50 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.

name: Doughnuts
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, 75g sugar and salt, then add the butter, eggs and warm milk. Knead for 10 minutes until smooth.
Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour. Divide into 12 balls and prove on a floured tray for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil to 170C and fry the doughnuts for 2 minutes each side until golden. Drain on kitchen paper.
Toss in the remaining sugar, then pipe jam into each doughnut.

name: Shortbread
steps: Heat the oven to 160C and line a baking tray.
Mix the flour, cornflour and 75g sugar, then rub in the butter and bring together into a dough.
Press into a 20cm round, prick with a fork, mark into 12 wedges and chill for 15 minutes.
Bake for 30 minutes until pale golden. Sprinkle with the remaining sugar and cool on the tray.

name: Chocolate chip cookies
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line two baking trays.
Beat the butter and both sugars until fluffy, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Stir in the flour, bicarbonate of soda and chocolate chips.
Drop 16 spoonfuls onto the trays, spaced apart, and bake for 12 minutes until golden at the edges.

name: Oat cookies
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line two baking trays.
Beat the butter and sugar until fluffy, then beat in the egg.
Stir in the flour, oats, bicarbonate of soda, cinnamon and raisins.
Place 16 spoonfuls on the trays, flatten slightly and bake for 12 minutes until golden.

name: Ginger biscuits
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line two baking trays.
Mix the flour, ginger and bicarbonate of soda, then rub in the butter and stir in the sugar.
Add the golden syrup and egg yolk and mix to a dough. Roll into 20 balls and flatten slightly on the trays.
Bake for 12 minutes until golden and cracked. Cool on the tray to crisp up.

name: Gingerbread men
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line two trays. Mix the flour, ginger and bicarbonate of soda and rub in the butter. Stir in the sugar.
Beat the golden syrup with the egg and mix into the dry ingredients to make a dough.
Roll out to 5mm thick, cut out figures and place on the trays.
Bake for 12 minutes until golden, cool, then mix the icing sugar with a little water and pipe on faces and buttons.

name: Jammy dodgers
steps: Beat the butter and icing sugar, then beat in the yolk and vanilla. Mix in the flour to make a dough and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180C. Roll out the dough and cut 24 rounds with a 6cm cutter.
Cut a small heart from the middle of half the rounds.
Bake for 10 minutes until pale golden. Cool, spread the whole biscuits with jam and top with the cut-out ones.

name: Viennese whirls
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line two trays.
Beat the first measure of butter and 50g icing sugar until pale, then mix in the flour, cornflour and vanilla.
Pipe 24 rosettes onto the trays with a star nozzle and bake for 15 minutes until pale golden. Cool.
Beat the remaining butter and icing sugar for the buttercream. Sandwich pairs of biscuits with the buttercream and a little jam.

name: Empire biscuits
steps: Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then mix in the yolk and flour to make a dough. Chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180C. Roll out to 4mm thick and cut 20 rounds with a 6cm cutter.
Bake for 12 minutes until pale golden, then cool.
Sandwich pairs with jam, mix the icing sugar with a little water, spread over the tops and finish each with half a cherry.

name: Digestive biscuits
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line two trays.
Mix the flours, oatmeal, baking powder, sugar and salt, then rub in the butter.
Add the milk to make a firm dough, roll out to 4mm and cut into 20 rounds. Prick with a fork.
Bake for 15 minutes until golden and cool on a rack.

name: Anzac biscuits
steps: Heat the oven to 160C and line two trays.
Mix the flour, oats, coconut and sugar.
Melt the butter and golden syrup, stir the bicarbonate of soda into the boiling water and add to the butter. Pour into the dry mix and stir.
Roll into 16 balls, flatten on the trays and bake for 12 minutes until golden.

name: Custard creams
steps: Heat the oven to 170C and line two trays.
Beat the first measure of butter and the sugar, then mix in the egg, flour and 25g of the custard powder to make a dough. Chill for 20 minutes.
Roll out to 4mm thick, cut 32 rectangles and bake for 12 minutes. Cool.
Beat the remaining butter, icing sugar, the rest of the custard powder and vanilla into a filling and sandwich the biscuits.

name: White loaf
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and sugar, rub in the butter and add the warm water to make a dough.
Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, then cover and leave to rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Knock back, shape and place in a greased 900g loaf tin. Cover and prove for 45 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220C and bake for 30 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped. Cool on a rack.

name: Wholemeal loaf
steps: Mix the flour, yeast and salt, then rub in the butter. Stir the treacle into the warm water and add to make a dough.
Knead for 10 minutes, then cover and leave to rise for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Shape into a loaf, place in a greased 900g tin and prove for 45 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220C and bake for 35 minutes until the loaf sounds hollow when tapped. Cool on a rack.

name: Soda bread
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and dust a baking tray with flour.
Mix the flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt in a bowl, then pour in the buttermilk and mix quickly to a soft dough.
Shape into a round on the tray and cut a deep cross in the top.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped. Cool on a rack.

name: Bread rolls
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and sugar, then rub in the butter and add the warm milk to make a dough. Knead for 10 minutes.
Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 12 balls, place on trays and prove for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220C, brush with egg and bake for 15 minutes until golden.

name: Crumpets
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then whisk in the milk and water to a thick batter. Cover and leave for 1 hour until bubbly.
Dissolve the bicarbonate of soda in 2 tbsp warm water and stir into the batter. Rest for 10 minutes.
Grease a frying pan and 8 metal crumpet rings with oil and heat the pan on a medium-low heat.
Fill each ring with batter about 1.5cm deep and cook for 6 minutes until the top is set and full of holes. Flip for 1 minute. Toast and butter to serve.

name: English muffins
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and sugar, rub in the butter and add the milk to make a soft dough. Knead for 10 minutes.
Cover and rise for 1 hour. Roll out to 2cm thick and cut 8 rounds with a 9cm cutter.
Dust with semolina and leave to prove for 30 minutes.
Cook in a dry frying pan over a low heat for 8 minutes each side until golden and cooked through. Split and toast to serve.

name: Bagels
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and the first measure of sugar with the warm water. Knead for 10 minutes and leave to rise for 1 hour.
Divide into 8 balls, poke a hole through each and stretch to a ring. Rest for 15 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220C. Boil a large pan of water with the remaining sugar and poach the bagels for 1 minute each side.
Brush with egg, sprinkle with sesame seeds and bake for 20 minutes until golden.

name: Cheese and onion bread
steps: Fry the onion in the oil for 8 minutes until soft and leave to cool.
Mix the flour, yeast and salt, rub in the butter and add the warm water. Knead for 10 minutes.
Knead in the onion and 100g of the cheddar. Cover and rise for 1 hour.
Shape into a loaf, place on a tray, scatter with the remaining cheddar and prove for 30 minutes.
Bake at 200C for 35 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding.

name: Tiger bread
steps: Mix the flour, first measure of yeast, salt and sugar, then add the sesame oil and warm water. Knead for 10 minutes and rise for 1 hour.
Shape into a round or oblong loaf, place on a tray and prove for 30 minutes.
Stir the rice flour, sugar, remaining yeast, oil and 100ml warm water into a paste and leave for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220C. Spread the paste thickly over the loaf and bake for 30 minutes until the topping cracks and the bread is golden.
